reviews.text:
I was very impressed with Thor’s Sourdough Bakery & Coffee - Tan Thanh beach.

The restaurant/bakery is very spacious and has a relaxed vibe to it. There are 2 floors - the main is where people can chitchat and the 2nd floor is a “quiet” area. Overall, the restaurant was extremely clean and pleasant.

The staff were super friendly and welcoming. Our order doubled checked and brought out promptly.

We ordered the chicken pesto sourdough sandwich and the ham & cheese croissant sandwich….both were absolutely amazing!!! The bread was flaky, the veggies were fresh and every bite was full of flavour. We also ordered the tropical smoothie and coconut iced coffee - both were delicious.

The bakery is well air conditioned and has 2 bathrooms on each floor. There is free Wi-Fi available. There is also patio seating available outside.

I highly recommend this place and I will definitely be back here again soon - enjoy 😊

Our last day in Hoi An and we saved this treasure for our first and last brunch and it did not dissappoint! The home made pesto is 🔥, croissants are buttery and amazing! Everything was a standout! I can’t say enough about how good the food was and it’s a beautiful space with staff who cook with intention!

I love when a space lives up to the hype and more! 😊

It was soooo good I had to come back! I had their egg + avo toast both times and also tried their pain au chocolate! It was spot on, very fresh and filling as a brunch meal. Their sourdough is very delicious and used for their sandwiches I believe. Their bowls looks absolutely good as well but haven’t had the chance to try. The location is amazing, quiet and great to work if you need to as well. Highly recommend!!!

reviewContext.Vegetarian options: There’s definitely some delicious vegetarian options!

reviews.text:
We’ve been in Hoi An for a few weeks, and this is by far the nicest place to have breakfast/lunch and work. The staff is super friendly, and the coffee is great. But what really makes it special is the free water, perfect for staying hydrated when you're working all day!

They also serve delicious sourdough, and yes, there is air conditioning and there is good wifi. There wasn't even any music playing, making it completely quiet and peaceful. I honestly don't have a single idea on how to improve this place for digital nomads.

We’ve spent many hours here.
Thank you 💛🫰

We stopped in on our last morning here at A Bang Beach, unfortunately, because we would have come here every morning. The Ham and Cheese on Sourdough is a must. I imagine everything here is the same level of 10/10. We also got the chocolate strawberry cake, coconut coffee, salty coffee and we had to try the protein shake. This place is amazing. All of these came out quick and are best in class execution.
The atmosphere here is just like an upscale laid back beachside cafe should be, the AC is perfect, and we left wanting more.
Cheers Thom’s!

came here for lunch during a trip to the beach and it was amazing! the indoors is air conditioned which is so lovely. we ordered the cheese toastie, veggie protein bowl, berry smoothie and a coffee all were delicious. the staff were very friendly and only a short walk from the beach.

reviewContext.Vegetarian options: lots of veggie options and even a choice to make certain dishes vegan

And on top of that, the prices are very good for the quality you get.
The kind of place you come to for breakfast and leave already feeling energized and happy. 100% recommend!

reviews.text:
A magical Frezeedom experience.
I went to this delightful ice cream spot in Hoi An and was absolutely enchanted from the first scoop to the last. The customer service here is genuinely exceptional—what truly made my visit unforgettable was the gentle, lovely lady who warmly greeted me and took the time to chat.

Each scoop had this wonderfully playful, artisanal quality—you can tell these aren't just standard flavors but carefully crafted experiences. The textures were silky, the tastes were vibrant and balanced, and there was a genuine sense of creativity in every bite.

What could have been a quick dessert stop turned into one of the highlights of my trip, thanks to both the extraordinary ice cream and the heartfelt hospitality. If you're in Hoi An, do yourself a favor and visit this gem. Come for the whimsical flavors, stay for the warm, personal touch. I'll definitely be back!

p.s: I ate mango and passion fruit ice cream (vegan) and jaggery dark choco (with authentic Vietnamese chocolate).

A definite must try!!!

We had key lime cheesecake, candied hazelnut salted caramel, honeycomb and rum raisin. They were all so good. A definite must try!!! If you like nuts and a slight saltiness to the sweet, try the hazelnut. We actually wanted to try the tiramisu but it is soooo sold out. Quite a lot were but these that were had were amazing!!! Such good quality and they put in so much thought and attention to detail. In every cup!!!

The staff are super friendly and lovely! This is a local handcrafted ice cream shop, so there are plenty of flavors to choose from. I especially love the fruity ones like plum cider and MC  — try them with salted!! Trust me, it's an amazing combo. Yah definitely worth a try!

The best ice cream spot in Hoi An for sure and I’m glad I found the spot. The tiramisu ice cream was amazing. Art and feel of the shop was great and lastly the person who served us with the cool tattoos was the nicest person as well as another lovely waiter I met who is also a chef. It gives a comforting feel and I hope to be back again the next time I’m in Vietnam.

I had the keylime cheesecake and young coconut ice creams and they were delish. Their selections are interesting and I'd love to come back to try more. Alex, the lady who assisted us, was lovely and welcoming. They have an ice cream jenga in the shop which was fun to play with. Highly recommended!
Very good icecream with a lot of interesting flavours! The staffmember we met was so kind and attentive!!! We will come back

This is the best ice cream I have ever tried! 🍦
The café in Hoi An makes handmade ice cream using only natural ingredients – no artificial colors or added sugar, just pure flavor. There is a huge variety of flavors: from fresh and slightly tangy to rich and sweet.

The highlight is the owner herself. She explains each flavor with so much care: what it’s made of, what it will taste like, whether it’s more on the sweet side or has a refreshing tang. Every detail is described so clearly and with love for her craft.

The staff are incredibly friendly, and the atmosphere is warm and welcoming. This place definitely deserves not just 5, but 10 stars ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐.

Highly recommended to anyone visiting Hoi An – you won’t regret it!
They had so many flavors to choose from, and the server Alex was so kind. The ice cream was really good as well. I got the mangosteen and soursop sorbet, and it was absolutely delightful!
reviews.responseFromOwnerText:

The Mangosteen & Soursop sorbet is one of our favorite seasonal flavor as well, and we’re glad it hit the spot for you. Hope to welcome you back soon to hangout and try even more flavors!

With love,
Freezedom Team

reviews.text:
A local gem for chiken rice lovers! 🍗🍚

We ate at Cơm Gà Cô MỲ and it was a treat from start to finish. The chicken rice was absolutely delicious: the chicken was tender and flavorful, the rice was perfectly seasoned, and everything was just right.

The place has a real local atmosphere, no frills, with a friendly and authentic vibe. You eat on small chairs in a simple but very pleasant setting.

The staff are super friendly, smiling and welcoming—you can feel their genuine passion for cooking and desire to please.
Excellent value for money and a genuine Vietnamese culinary experience.

I recommend it 100% if you're in the area!

I saw this little chicken and rice stand with a little row of seating down the alley.  I just love little gems like this serving great local dishes out in the outdoors.  This place must be a stop of local street food because I could overhear local foodie guides explaining things to the people their were with :).  The food was fresh....rice wasn't overcooked and the chicken was great.  The owner pointed out to squeeze a lime over top, put some chili sauce on top, and good covering of soya sauce.  Very tasty plate of food for $1.50 Canadian....25000VND.  You can tell the owners take pride in their food and we're very happy when I gave them the thumbs up 👍😀.

Was the only foreign person eating there. Locals flock this spot to eat in or order for takeaway. The people who run this cart are very friendly and accommodating too, even prepared the dish with the correct seasonings after serving it. Great value comfort food, must try in Hoi An

If you don't look out for the name on its food cart, you might miss it. Owners are a friendly husband and wife team. We came about half hour after they had opened, so it was quiet but the chicken rice was amazingly fresh. The chicken intestine/offal side that came with it was really tasty and well seasoned. The rice was also really light that it didnt make you feel heavy, and we could've easily went for a second plate. Great price for a banger meal.

The Com Ga is AMAZING. So amazing that we ordered one servicing then got a second one. Com Ga is chicken and rice that is served with herbs and salad. They also give you broth on the side and have limes and chilis to add to your dish.

It was 30k for 1 serving which was some of the most affordable food we’ve had in Hoi An.

I will be thinking about this meal for a while and will have to resort to attempting to recreate it at home since I’m leaving Vietnam soon.

This is the best Com Ga  (chicken rice), I found in Hoi An. Very nice lady with her little cart with several spots lined up to sit along side. Im so happy I went back for another look. Soo fresh and very very good. No wait!!
An amazingly good $1 meal—authentic to the core. You get to eat on tiny tables and chairs by the street, comfortably shaded and very windy. The madam and the gentleman were incredibly friendly.

I just left this place and wow. The dish is so good, and the best part was the homemade chili sauce. I bought some to take home. Such a flavorful dish, and the chicken was so tender. Not at all like some reviews I read at the “legendary” places. You have to check this spot out on your trip to Hoi An!

Nhà hàng hải sản Tam Giang ở công viên cồn tộc (Quảng Điền) là nơi tôi hay tiếp bạn bè. Không chỉ đồ ăn ngon, tươi sống, đa dạng menu, mà còn có giá thành hợp ví tiền. Hihi.

reviews.textTranslated: A great place to enjoy quality seafood from the Tam Giang lagoon, with a spacious and airy atmosphere, beautiful views, and delicious food. Definitely worth a visit.
reviews.text: Một địa điểm thưởng thức hải sản đầm phá tam Giang chất lượng, không gian thoáng mát, nhà hàng có view đẹp, đồ ăn ngon nữa chứ. Xứng đáng ghé lại quán này.

reviews.textTranslated: While enjoying a trip to Tam Giang Lagoon and paddling a SUP (stand-up paddleboard) to admire the beautiful scenery, I saw a restaurant sign and decided to try it out. reviews.text:
After being recommended by our hotel, we decided to try this restaurant—just note that it’s located upstairs above another restaurant, so it can be a little easy to miss.

They offer both Vietnamese and Western food, but we stuck with the Vietnamese options. It’s located right opposite a nightclub, which actually made for some pretty entertaining people-watching while we dined. You can choose to sit outside or downstairs in air conditioning.

We started with the papaya salad, which was very good—served with peanuts and dried onions—though not quite as fresh as what we experienced during a cooking class in Hoi An. The standout dish was definitely the eggplant with garlic and butter—absolutely amazing and a must-order.

We also had the beef hot pot, which came with very rare slices of beef that you cook yourself, along with vegetables and rice noodles. It was a fun and interactive meal.

Overall, a really nice experience, and great value at around 350,000.

reviews.text:
Legit the best bahn mi I've had on my trip. The #5 Roast Pork or Bahn Mi Thit Heo Quay was really good. The large size is a foot long or so. It's not stuffed to the brim with fillings, but I think that is a point in its favor, as it balances well with the bread. Sesame seeds on the bread.

The older couple at the place we're kind, and spoke enough English to ask if wanted it spicy and if we wanted pate.

They toast the bread, and it's crispy with a delightful chew. We got ours to-go, but there was a little eating space if you wish.

The food was simply amazing! we tried the big pork roast bahn mi at was a 15/10!!!! Just absolutely tasty and delicious! The place is very simple and local but the lady is super sweet and lets you choose all the ingredients of your bahn mi! and we spent only 99 cents each which is absolutely crazy!

Had a roast pork Banh Mi here yesterday. Probably the best banh mi and I've had a few all over Vietnam. Moist pork,just the right amount of veg and fantastic bread,toasted with sesame seeds on top.I returned today for the chicken nugget banh mi and that was great too. Friendly couple with good English running the place

Bánh Mì Chu Văn An is an absolute must-visit if you want to experience what a real Vietnamese bánh mì should taste like. It’s a small, humble street stall — nothing fancy at all — but what comes out of that tiny setup is pure perfection.
I ordered the special bánh mì, and honestly, it was the best bánh mì I’ve ever had. It comes loaded with everything — different types of meats, pate, pickled vegetables, herbs, sauces — and the combination is just brutal. Every bite is perfectly balanced: crunchy bread, rich and savory fillings, and that signature mix of sweet, salty, and slightly tangy flavors that make Vietnamese sandwiches so unique.
The bread was perfectly toasted — light and crisp on the outside, soft and warm inside — and it held together beautifully without falling apart, even with all those delicious fillings. The ingredients were incredibly fresh, and the sauce tied everything together just right. You can tell this is made by someone who knows exactly what they’re doing.
The woman who runs the stall is one of the kindest and warmest people I’ve met while traveling in Vietnam. She was super friendly and welcoming, smiling the entire time and clearly proud of her food. Even though her English was limited, communication wasn’t a problem — her kindness said it all. You can feel the love and care she puts into every sandwich.
The price is also fantastic — incredibly cheap for the quality and size of the sandwich. It’s one of those meals that makes you stop and think, “How can something this good cost so little?” You could easily pay three times as much elsewhere and not come close to this level of flavor or satisfaction.
What I loved most was that this isn’t a tourist trap — it’s a genuine, local spot serving real food for real people. There’s no marketing gimmick, no fancy decor — just honest, homemade perfection.
If you only have time to try one bánh mì while in Vietnam, make it this one. The special is the way to go — it’s got a little bit of everything, and the combination is absolutely spot-on.
The location is easy to find, and even if you have to wait a few minutes during busy hours, it’s completely worth it. Everything is made fresh, right in front of you, and the result is unforgettable.
Overall, Bánh Mì Chu Văn An is everything you want in a Vietnamese street-food experience: incredible flavor, friendly people, and unbeatable value. The special bánh mì is out of this world — truly the best I’ve had anywhere.

Friendly service and a decent Bánh mi. Very average compared to the several banh mi I devoured during my Vietnam trip. The lady and her husband I assume are very helpful and friendly though and pointed me to their neighbor for drinks while I waited the few seconds it took for the banh mi to be prepared. The prices are on the lower side for banh mi and they were not bad at all.

A relaxing experience

As the name suggests, the cafe is located inside the famous Vi Da Hamlet. It is roomier than it looks with the backyard right next to the river, which offers a great view and calm asmotsphere.

I order one salted coffee and a set of imperial tea.

The coffee is great. The sweetness and saltiness of the cream complement the bitterness of the coffee, resulting in a sophisticated and well-rounded flavour profile.

Next is the tea set.
For an affordable price, this is one of the best tea experiences you can find. The brew features dried fruits and is served with a side of sweets to complement the flavors. Each sip offers a subtle bitterness and sweet aftertaste that finishes with a fragant herbal notes.

Last but not least, the employees are super friendly who carefully attend to your needs.

I have come here ever since I was young. It’s my favourite breakfast spot. A little on the more expensive side but the breakfast dishes are delicious. The yoghurt drinks are my favourite too. Hanh, our waitress gave us a great service.

5 star is not enough, I could give more if I could! Food portion servings were huge and affordable for an ambience like this! Great view of the river outside but I came when it was raining so I opted to sit at the building outside to have tea and sweets. Had dinner at the dining hall which was behind. The 149k VND tea set for 2 pax was the best experience ever! Peaceful surroundings with plants and background music, great deco and lighting, good tea and snacks!
Recommended when you’re in Hue!

On a beautiful day during a family road trip from North to South, we stopped here for lunch. The space is beautiful and peaceful, and the dining room facing the river offers a very nice and breezy view. The food is well-seasoned and nicely presented. If you happen to visit Hue, this is definitely a reasonable choice for you and your family.

They have coffee and drink along with breakfast, afternoon tea, and traditional Hue dinner. I tried and the taste is authentic. If you come to Hue, do not miss this place. The back yard is riverfront. Great view. Be mindful with mosquitos though. I will come again when i visit Hue.

. You have to come here when you visit Hue 🤍

What an absolute gem of a coffee spot. It’s tucked away in a quiet little alley, run by the whole family, and their kids are honestly the cutest. It feels like a true local, hip coffee space — thoughtfully curated, relaxed, and authentic. The kind of place where you can really slow down and enjoy your time.

We tried the salted coffee and the black sesame coffee (the first time we’ve ever seen that!), and both were so good — unique, balanced, and beautifully made. They also host coffee workshops, and even though we were only in Hue for one day during Lunar New Year and didn’t have enough time, this is absolutely where we would have chosen to do one.

At night, it transforms into a cozy bar. We came back for live music during Lunar New Year, and it was such a special experience. The atmosphere, the music, the warmth — we were welcomed so wholeheartedly. It was the perfect way to end our visit to Hue.

If you’re looking for something genuine, local, and memorable — this is the place

reviews.text:
We had such a wonderful experience, made even better by the fantastic service from Amy. She was incredibly friendly and attentive, always greeting us with a beautiful smile and making sure we had everything we needed.

Amy took the time to explain the dishes and showed us the best way to enjoy and eat the different foods, which really added to our experience of Vietnamese cuisine. Her attention to detail was fantastic, and nothing ever felt like too much trouble.

The cocktails were absolutely marvellous too! 🍹

Amy's warm personality, genuine friendliness and excellent service really stood out to us. She made our evening feel special and is a wonderful asset to the restaurant. Thank you, Amy, for looking after us so well during our time in Huế. Highly recommended! ❤️

I don't get where all these overwhelmingly positive reviews came from. Place is clean and pretty, but food is very very average. Taco Ban Xeo - cold, steam vegetables cold, clay pot chicken almost bland, fish soup pretty good. If you expect great food - find other place nearby. If you expect to sit and chill, it's pretty and drinks are good. For price above average food is below average. Honestly - don't recommend, not a restaurant level. Service was good, but waiter asked to take our unfinished food, why?

A all round 5 star restaurant, from the point of reservation to being welcomed to the restaurant, service was thoughtful and friendly. Every dish was infused with flavour, beautifully presented and just yummy. The sou vide duck breast was a masterpiece. The herbal tea is delicious and recommended for herbal tea lovers.  The upstairs area was closed yesterday evening but the team turned on the lights and welcomed us to go and tour the beautifully designed upstairs with emperor chairs and portraits. Overall a perfect dining experience and will return if in Hue again.

This is what fine dining should be in Vietnam. Best duck ever! Chicken sauce is a bit spicy but delicious. Drinks are perfect and coffee is an experience. Staff is wonderful and happy to help. Overall great experience. Thanks for this nice evening.
A bit pricy but worth it.

reviews.text: This was an exceptional experience. The food was great. The waitor Darwin was a lovely man that treated us well. Mong is the nicest and most beautiful woman and was really kind to us. The food was great and they went above and beyond. An definately must see and Hue. The restaurant looks great and even the bathrooms were the cleanest i have seen in Vietnam . They are really lovely people. I will visit them again no doubt.

Husband save the night.. with help from this place. Today was one of those days when you just don't want anything. He insisted, and it paid off. I was not hungry, but a taste of the dishes change my mood. The beef tartar and the grilled prawn with grapefruit side... Wonderful. We had just appetizers but it worked so we could try different dishes. In addition the mocktals, really refreshing and tasty!! Andrew was so welcoming and helpful. We'll try to repeat!

Lovely experience at Vi Hue! I had the fresh spring rolls for entree and the slow cooked pork with sticky rice for main. Everything was delicious!! Also had a cocktail served in a coconut which was tasty and fun. Our server Rosa was great, friendly and attentive. Would recommend visiting for those in Hue.

I came here with great expectations cuz of the reviews and was left feeling a bit disappointed. Appetisers and drink were great! The pork balls and lotus salad were delicious. Pork jowl and chicken that had the recommended symbol in the menu were just so so. The glutinous rice that came with both were abit hard and bland. Pork jowl tasted quite nice on its own. Cocktail was good! Love their ginger tea as well.

We decided to gamble on a random local diner and this place has officially topped our must-have restaurants/diners list.
This is not just your regular diner whatsoever, as a Vietnamese person myself, I was absolutely blown away by HOW tasty the food was. Oh and mind you, this was our first time traveling to Huế, so this was definitely our lucky-pick right after we got off the train lol.

reviews.text: We ate brunch at Nina’s cafe and loved it so much we just had to come back the next day again! The smoothie bowls and fresh juices were so refreshing, we couldn’t believe this amazing spot was just tucked away in a little alley very close to our hotel. Our waitresses, Nhi and Moon, were amazing: they made us feel very welcome and spoke great english as well. We couldn’t recommend this place more for a quick brunch!

If you are looking for the absolute best food in Vietnam, look no further than Nina’s Cafe. We came in for a late brunch that effortlessly turned into a long, delicious lunch—and honestly, we didn’t want to leave. After three weeks of traveling through the country, this was hands-down the best food and selection we’ve encountered.
​The atmosphere is incredibly relaxing and cozy, providing the perfect escape from the bustle of the city. However, what truly elevates this experience from a great meal to an unforgettable one is the hospitality. Our host, Ms. Lotus, was perfection. Her English is impeccable, and she is so much more than just a host; she is a cultural ambassador. She took the time to sit with us and educate us on the traditional way to prepare and eat each dish, adding a layer of depth to the meal that you just don't find elsewhere.
​We will be back again for sure. If you’re in Hue, do yourself a favor and find this hidden gem!

Finding Nina’s Cafe at the end of a long, quiet alleyway is half the fun—the other half is the incredible food and hospitality. This small, cozy spot is a peaceful escape from the main streets.

​The Service:
Huge shoutout to Lotus, who was a total powerhouse. She was the only server managing the entire restaurant single-handedly, yet she stayed welcoming, spoke excellent English, and took a genuine interest in our trip. Her recommendations were spot-on.

​The Standout Dishes:
​The BBQ Pork Noodles (Bun Thit Nuong): The pork had a fantastic flavor that reminded me of Filipino tocino, and the peanut sauce was the perfect finishing touch.

​Set 1: An absolute steal for the price. The Banh Beo was incredibly fresh, and the Banh Nam was a delicious highlight I’m glad we tried.

​Fried Fish: Light, crispy, and perfectly battered. It let the quality of the fish shine through instead of overpowering it.
​Grilled Lemon Chicken: This was "booming" with flavor—a massive hit with my son.

​If you want an authentic, quiet meal with top-tier service, make sure you find your way down the alley to this gem.

Nina’s café is a true gem, tucked away in a narrow street in central Hué. Do not hesitate to visit. The place feels fresh and welcoming, creating a lovely atmosphere from the moment you arrive.

Moon and N were extremely friendly and helped us choose our dishes with great care. They also speak excellent English, which is not always the case in many restaurants and cafés in Hué.

The food itself was delicious, beautifully presented, and very reasonably priced. The drinks were equally impressive, with great attention to detail in their presentation.

Highly recommended ☺️

One of our favourite restaurants of our trip - we ate here twice during our 2 nights in Hue. The caramel chicken hot pot is a must have but everything we tried was delicious.
Lee was attentive and helpful explaining the dishes. A must go if you are visiting Hue.

reviews.text: Absolutely fantastic experience! The food here is insanely delicious, full of authentic flavor, and prepared with super fresh ingredients. I loved that they have great options for different dietary needs, including a dedicated gluten free menu and plenty of thoughtful vegan choices. We ordered a spread of amazing dishes and were blown away. The crispy Thai fried chicken served on banana leaf with kaffir lime leaves was incredible, and the fried chicken over rice with fresh cucumber slices was equally delicious. We also loved the stir fried noodles, the savory seafood fried rice with fresh lime wedges, and the cashew stir fry. Everything was packed with flavor, beautifully cooked, and loaded with fresh ingredients. Highly recommend this spot to anyone looking for amazing Thai food!

Really tasty Thai street food with vegan and veggie options, close to my accommodation - I came here a lot over my 10 days or so in Hue. Could easily eat here every day as it is so good - nourishing, healthy, generous portions and great value. Very handy as it stays open until 11pm, so if you’re back late or it’s rainy season, it’s perfect to have so close by. The service is fantastic and the meals are made so quickly, you can be in and out in 20-30 minutes usually. Everything was fresh to order and so delicious and you can see the cooks doing their thing in the kitchen. The place was always packed with locals and tourists alike but they will always find space for you. A great atmosphere as always busy, and you sit around quite communal with small tables close together and small chairs. They have a vegan menu of their regular dishes that can be adapted - so I had a lot of stir fried cashew nuts, tofu and vegetables on rice in various seasoning and sauces. They always check no fish sauce and no egg, and also ask your spice preference. Every combination I tried was 10/10. Very consistently good. They also sell bottled water and beers etc.

reviews.text:
Best meal we’ve had in Vietnam! After being disappointed by overpriced “fine dining” at other luxury resorts—where the food and atmosphere fell far below expectations, we decided to try Le Parfum at Azerai Hue. Knowing the hotel is owned by Adrian Zecha, the founder of Aman Resorts, we anticipated something special, and it delivered beyond our expectations.

The food was not only of exceptional quality but also reasonably priced for a luxury experience. The lamb rack was perfectly cooked and packed with flavor, the duck breast was tender and delicious, and the dessert trilogy crème brûlée was a unique treat with durian, hibiscus, and coffee flavors, all executed to perfection. Even the Vietnamese dishes were elevated, showcasing the chef’s skill and attention to detail.

If you’re looking for a true fine dining experience in central Vietnam, skip the hype elsewhere and head to Le Parfum at Azerai Hue. The food, service, and overall experience were leagues ahead of what we’ve experienced at other so-called luxury restaurants. Highly recommended!

The food is delicious, especially the bánh xèo, which stands out as a must-try dish. The staff is very attentive and goes above and beyond to ensure a pleasant dining experience. The restaurant also features live piano music, adding a romantic and elegant touch to the atmosphere. Located within a hotel, the restaurant offers a stunning view of the Hương River, making the setting even more picturesque and charming. I highly recommend this place for anyone looking to enjoy great food, excellent service, and a beautiful, serene environment.
We had a late lunch today and it was delicious. We chose outdoor seating as the weather was perfect. Great service and delicious food. Highly recommend visiting this place for lunch or dinner.

We had an awesome upscale experience at the restaurant. The food was phenomenal, and the wagyu was out of this world. The chef Cuc really did a fantastic job. and the restaurant manager Phuong was super nice and forthcoming. We would definitely be back here on our nest stay in Hue.
Really excellent food and a short but well crafted wine list. Would thoroughly recommend

I booked a table for six people. This is one of the best restaurants in Vietnam. If there were six stars, I would rate at six stars. The service,  the staff, the food was excellent. I would recommend everyone when in Hue, definitely you have to make this a must place to dine.
We came only for drinks and dessert, it was perfect!

Hello, thanks for the dinner. Everything was nice and good.
Service was perfect.

reviews.text: We stopped in for a late breakfast with the family and couldn’t have been happier with the choice. The food was delicious, hearty, and left us completely satisfied. My kids devoured everything on their plates and even asked to come back the next day. Service was quick and attentive — they nailed my request for extra crispy bacon in the sandwich. The bread was wonderfully fresh, and the chilled orange juice was perfectly refreshing.

Love this place! I've come back 4 times now. Their food is so tasty and has great flavour.
The Shakshuka was awesome with a massive bread roll, the mixed omlette, Vietnamese rice pancake and the Chicken Pho are incredible- one of my favourite Pho in Vietnam so far. So flavoursome!
The owners are the sweetest ladies and are always happy to see you ☺️. They even thanked me for coming back and gifted me a plate of mango to say farewell on my last visit 🥹. They really appreciate you supporting their restaurant.
Such a great place with the best people who now feel like family. Love the dining area at the top, very open and natural 😍.

Family Home Café & Restaurant was one of those happy discoveries in Hue that turned into a genuine favourite. We ended up eating here several times during our stay, which really says it all. When a place pulls you back that consistently, it's doing something right.
The pho is wonderful — comforting, well-balanced, and exactly what you want after a day of exploring. But what surprised us was the shakshuka. Rich, flavourful, and totally unexpected on a Vietnamese café menu — it works brilliantly and we'd order it every time. Pair either with a cold beer in that cozy, relaxed setting and you've got yourself a near-perfect meal.
The atmosphere is warm and unpretentious, the kind of place that feels lived-in and welcoming rather than curated for tourists. It's easy to linger here, and we did — often. The staff play a big part in that. They're genuinely lovely, attentive without being intrusive, and add to the overall feeling that this is a place run with real care.
If you're spending time in Hue, put Family Home on your list early — that way you'll have plenty of chances to go back. Five stars without hesitation.

reviews.text: Absolutely lovely!! Homemade fresh food full of flavour. One of the best meals I had in Vietnam. The place is a nice family home with super friendly people

I love Family Home Restaurant! Everytime I visit, I feel warmly welcomed, as if I'm part of the family. The ladies treat me with genuine kindness and care, making each experience special. And of course, the food is consistently delicious, every dish was a delight. I recommend anything on menu! My favorite dishes are the Hue noodles with Fried Pork + Veg + Spring Rolls, Noodle Soup, or Báhn Mì. Also the smoothies are yummy too! This is my go-to place for comfort, good vibes, and great food!

-Miss Angie

We absolutely loved this restaurant!! We ended up coming back three times in just two days because the food was so delicious and the atmosphere so welcoming. They made us feel genuinely at home from the moment we arrived — it felt very warm and family-like.

The dishes were incredibly tasty and the prices were more than fair, which made the experience even better. If we hadn’t been leaving the city, we definitely would have come back again.

We can highly recommend this place to anyone looking for great food and a truly friendly atmosphere!
We went for dinner here one evening. I got the fried noodles with chicken and vegetables and the veg and tofu spring rolls. It was all very simple and very tasty.

We found this place by accident and saw that they had shakshuka - our favorite breakfast dish. We loved the place so much that we came back the next day.

It’s a really cute family business run out of their home. Very nice rooftop seating with good ambience and friendly service.

The food is fantastic. We tried shakshuka, banh mi chao, and a few other Vietnamese dishes. Everything was fresh and flavourful. The coffee and tea were also excellent.

If we lived in Hue, we would probably come here every weekend. I highly recommend it.

reviews.text: Great place for dinner & drinks and enjoy the sunset. Excellent selection of Vietnamese/French dishes. Great selection of wine/drinks. We started on the rooftop bar first then we came down to the restaurant to eat. Service is great. They have a lot of creative/fusion dishes to enjoy. There is something for everyone. It's on the pricey side but worth it. They open super early at 6am so you can also enjoy the sunrise if you choose to come there and have some breakfast. Rooftop bar doesn't have any food/snacks. Restaurant can get busy at times so I recommend booking in advance to snag the best table. Manager is fantastic and can explain everything to you in English.
reviews.responseFromOwnerText:
Dear Tab Dan,

Thank you very much for taking the time to share such a detailed and thoughtful review of Le Cercle!

We are delighted to hear that you enjoyed your time at our Rooftop Bar, followed by dinner at the restaurant, and that you appreciated our selection of Vietnamese and French dishes, creative fusion creations, wines, and drinks. It is wonderful to know that you found something to suit everyone and felt that the overall experience was well worth it.

We are also pleased that you enjoyed the sunset and appreciated the service provided by our team. Your kind words about our manager are especially appreciated, and we will certainly share your compliments with the team.

Thank you as well for highlighting some helpful tips for future guests. We truly appreciate your recommendation to book in advance, particularly for those hoping to enjoy one of our best tables.

It was a pleasure having you with us, and we hope to welcome you back to Le Cercle soon—perhaps for breakfast and a beautiful sunrise next time!

reviews.text:
Situated by the enchanting Perfume River in Hue, Le Circle is a fine dining gem that promises an unforgettable culinary experience. The restaurant boasts a beautiful terrace that provides the perfect backdrop for a relaxing dinner, especially as the sun sets over the river.

I had the pleasure of indulging in what was undoubtedly the most posh Wagyu beef pho I have ever tasted, utterly delicious! The flavors were rich and nuanced, showcasing the expertise behind the dish. The starters were equally impressive, with generous portion sizes that were both well-seasoned and packed with flavor.

Le Circle offers an extensive menu that features a wonderful selection of Vietnamese cuisine, as well as a broader array of Asian dishes. The variety ensures that there’s something for everyone, making it an ideal spot for group dining or special occasions.

What truly enhanced my experience was the attentive service. My waiter went above and beyond by assisting me in combining the pho ingredients, sharing the traditional rituals of preparing the dish. This personal touch offered a glimpse into the local culture and made the meal even more special.

In conclusion, Le Circle is a must-visit in Hue for anyone seeking a fine dining experience with exquisite food and a stunning setting. With its attentive service, delightful flavors, and picturesque views, it is a place I can’t wait to return to. Highly recommended!
reviews.responseFromOwnerText:

We are truly delighted to know that your experience at Le Cercle was both memorable and meaningful. Your description of the terrace overlooking the Perfume River at sunset perfectly captures the atmosphere we strive to create—refined, relaxing, and quietly captivating.

It is especially rewarding to hear your appreciation for our Wagyu beef pho. This signature dish reflects our culinary philosophy of elevating traditional flavors with a contemporary touch, and we are pleased that it stood out as a highlight of your dining experience. Your kind words about the starters and the variety of our menu are equally appreciated.

We are particularly grateful for your recognition of our service. The gesture of guiding you through the traditional way of enjoying pho is something our team takes pride in, as we aim not only to serve a meal, but also to share a cultural story with each guest.

Thank you once again for your generous recommendation. It would be our great pleasure to welcome you back to Le Cercle for another exceptional experience in the near future.

Warm regards,
Le Cercle Management Team

reviews.text: Absolutely loved this place! Their papaya salad is super fresh and flavorful, and the “chicken” salad (tofu) was a delicious surprise. The lemongrass tofu was nicely seasoned and satisfying. Everything tasted fresh, and the best part? Three meals for under 120K VND! Amazing value for such quality food. Definitely a spot worth checking out! ✅🌿

The BEST chay banh mi in all of Vietnam! Trust me, we’ve tried so many in different cities, but nothing compares to this. I literally just left, ate TWO of them, and I’m already craving more! Sending so much love, health, and prosperity to the wonderful ladies running this place. You are amazing! 💖💖💖

Awesome place! Been here twice.

Our favourite was the special banh mi - a definite must try. No extra descriptions needed. Just try it. For the generous price of 12.000 it alone is worth the visit.

hến trộn chay - a dish of minced green banana & seaweed was a real discovery. Seriously, NOT just an interesting yet “never try again” kind of dish, but actually very tasty. It was savory minced-meat type of dish, not sweet at all, and served with a cracker. Great texture + savory taste, crunchy nuts and small slices of chilli. Recommend this one, don’t let it fly under your radar.

And I even liked stuffed gummy tapioca starch dumplings, which i don’t usually like, but here they were to my liking and were served with a cool chilli water sauce.

Prices are generous and the ladies working at this place are very nice too.
👍good taste , average price. polite shop lady 👍

Delicious vegetarian/vegan banh mi’s to die for. Smaller than usual, but extremely good value for money (10k price per) allowing to order multiple different ones to snack your way through the menu.

The owners (I think three women’s) are lovely and very kind. You can order for take away or eat there and they will put out a table and some tiny chairs :)

Make sure to not arrive too late before closing time, because in our case they sold out except for two breads. Nevertheless it was so good we ate there two days in a row.

Buddhist vegetarians who abstain from the five pungent spices (ngũ vị tân, e.g. onion, garlic, etc.) would love this place! Although the restaurant does serve food with the five pungent spices, the restaurant owner, Tạo, is a practicing Buddhist and perfectly understands this dietary requirement. He speaks good English and can advise you on which dishes can be made without the five pungent spices. We've dined in once and have been ordering in from him. The dishes we've ordered are tasty and have never tasted of the five pungent spices. This is pretty rare because most vegetarian restaurants in Vietnam just aren't sensitive enough to this dietary requirement.

We love the stir-fried mixed vegetables, braised tofu with tamarind sauce, braised straw mushrooms, sa te fried rice and more!

reviews.text:
Mr. Pho was a great experience! It’s the perfect place to get a snack/breakfast before taking the train.
The food is fresh and delicious! I can really recommend the Banh Mi with Omelette. The coffee is delicious as well!

The owner is very welcoming and friendly. It’s a pleasure to chat with him.
I can highly recommend this place.

If you arrive in Huế by train, you might easily walk past this small and very unassuming place, but that would be a mistake. Mr Pho’s Pho and Cafe looks simple at first glance: plastic chairs, plastic tables, exactly what you would expect from a typical local Vietnamese spot. But behind that simplicity is truly great food.

The fried rice and fried noodles are excellent, fresh, flavorful, and perfect after a long journey. The prices are also very fair.

What really makes this place special, though, is Mr Pho himself. He takes great care of his guests, helps with train connections, gives travel tips, and if he has a moment, he even shares a few stories. You don’t feel like a customer there, you feel like a welcome guest.

It’s also very convenient for travelers: he offers to prepare food for your train journey and can store your luggage if you need to kill some time before your next train.

A genuine and authentic spot right next to the train station in Huế. Anyone passing through should definitely stop by.
★★★★★

Mr. Pho’s Café is a wonderful little spot located right across from the Hue railway station. The place is run by a very friendly and genuinely helpful owner, who makes the whole experience even better. The food is tasty, fresh, and prepared with great care.

One of the things I appreciated most is how thoughtful the owner is. Before taking your order, he asks which train you’re waiting for to make sure the meal is ready in time. You can also order your food packed for the journey, which is perfect if you’re about to catch a train.

Overall, it’s a warm, reliable, and delicious stop in Hue—highly recommended, especially for travelers passing through the station.
Delicious food, quick service, very reasonable prices, good vegetarian options. If you arrive by train, it's right in front of the station. And they provide welcome drinks too! Highly recommended.

The guy who runs this establishment (maybe Mr Pho himself?) couldn't be any nicer. Located right by the train station, he looked after our bags for a very reasonable fee while we spent a day in Hue. He checked when our train was leaving, and told us which platform / waiting room we needed to be in. He was so nice and trusting, he voluntarily lent us cash because we'd run out, and said we could pay him back when we returned at the end of the day.

Because of his generosity, we stayed for a drink and some food, before heading towards the Imperial City. The banh mi were tasty and very reasonably priced.

Thank you for helping to make our visit to Vietnam an even better experience!
Mr Pho is one of the kindest person I've ever met, very helpful and nice. 100% recommended for storing luggage, eating or just traveling information.

Wow thank goodness for Mr Pho! I highly recommend this cafe! Their Banh mi is very nice and hearty!

My heritage train was cancelled (I found out at the station). Mr Pho helped me to book a VIP shuttle and made honest recommendations about places to visit in Hue and how to get around for the day.

I had stored my luggage with his family for a super reasonable fee, he takes his job seriously and I was so thankful to have met them.

Enjoyed a tasty veggie Pho as well as egg and veggie fried rice while sitting on the patio across from the train station. Friendly English speaking owner who gifted a glass of hot and iced tea. Excellent local pricing.

Follow me for more interesting updates!

i'be eaten here several times and my experiences have been great, when im lazy, i just order and they deliver to my house very fast. updatesFromCustomers.text: Huế mưa

reviews.text:
One of the BEST local food experiences we had in Hue! 🇻🇳❤️

Vietnamese Food - Hue Local Food & FastFood 22 Restaurant is honestly one of the best restaurants we found during our trip to Hue. It is located right in front of the Hue Imperial City, so it’s also a very convenient place to stop by while sightseeing.

We came here almost immediately after arriving in Hue, and we were so impressed that we already feel like we’ve found our “hidden gem” in Hue!

The owner was incredibly kind and welcoming, and the restaurant has cool air conditioning, which was such a relief after walking around in the hot and humid weather. Most importantly, every dish we ordered was delicious and tasted fresh and authentic.

We ordered Bún Bò Huế, Morning Glory, Bánh Cái, Bánh Nậm, a mango smoothie, and watermelon juice.

The little touches made the experience even better. We only ordered the Morning Glory, but they kindly gave us rice for free, and complimentary wet tissues were also provided.

And just when we thought we were finished and were about to leave, the owner surprised us with complimentary passion fruit and ginger tea as dessert! 🥭🍵

The food was delicious, the service was warm and genuinely friendly, the restaurant was clean and comfortable, and the prices were very reasonable.

If you're visiting Hue and want to try authentic local Vietnamese food in a comfortable, welcoming restaurant, I highly recommend stopping here.

We came in simply looking for a meal, but we left feeling like we had discovered a place we would happily come back to again.

If you're in Hue, put this restaurant on your list! You won't regret it. 👍👍👍👍👍

⭐ Delicious food
⭐ Friendly owner
⭐ Great value
⭐ Air-conditioned & comfortable
⭐ Generous complimentary extras
⭐ Perfect location near the Imperial City

Highly recommended! 🇻🇳❤️

reviews.text:
We visited Hue Imperial City and were looking for a halal-friendly restaurant nearby for lunch. We were very pleased to find An Nhien Garden Vegetarian.

The restaurant has a beautiful and peaceful ambience, with very friendly and helpful staff. The food was tasty and enjoyable.

A special thanks to Assistant Manager Hien Phu, who was very kind and helpful in arranging an alternative prayer area for us when the permanent prayer area was under maintenance. We truly appreciated the thoughtful hospitality and understanding.

Highly recommended for anyone visiting Hue, especially Muslim travellers looking for a welcoming and comfortable dining experience. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

What an absolutely beautiful and delicious restaurant. Don’t hesitate and book a table or make your way there now. The food was incredibly fresh and tasty but everything there has a wonderful back story to it. From the impetus for establishing the restaurant to the 400+ years of family legacy, there is so much to this place that you will not regret your decision to dine here.

The velvet apple or Hong Nhung was incredible if it’s in season when you’re there it’s a must. One of the best fruits I’ve ever tasted.

A truly hidden (!) gem. This is one of the must surprising, yet magical locations we‘ve seen in Vietnam. It‘s a backyard garden of a victorian style villa. My wife and my two kids loved it. Food was fantastic and not expensive. Perfect for everyone who‘s staying at the Kobi Onsen Resort.

I wish I had found this place on my last trip, but was super stoked to have found it on this trip to Hue.

The restaurant is set up in a garden with tables set up around it as well.

We started off sitting in the garden but there were some mosquitos so we moved away from the lush garden setting. Probably something that's hard to get away from as the weather warms up.

We ordered several platters with many things to try. One of my favorites was from "Hue on a Tray" where three different "banh" were offered. The black sesame item was exceptional both in taste and texture.

We also ordered the "Traditional Hue Meal" which included rice, veggies, tofu, soup, and a very unique pickled eggplant dish.

The Pomelo Salad was also very tasty.

I suggest making a reservation as the restaurant, though not full, was rather busy on a weeknight.

This is an incredible vegeterain place to eat. Caters for vegans and halal. Its the venue that makes the amazing food taste even better. The service is top notch. The meals in the pictures look smaller than they are, you might over-order.

Incredibly peaceful vegetarian/vegan garden refuge in the middle of Hue. The moment u walk in, you are greeted by hanging orchids, beautiful paintings, statue-adorned zen garden pathways, accompanied by the relaxing sound of water, leaves rustling, and birds singing along with cicadas. It's literally another world.

The staff was honest, polite & knowledgeable, so much that my aunt wanted to adopt one of them.

Although they are mostly vegan, some dishes may have milk, so make sure you ask the staff first. We were told everything on the menu can be made vegan. If you let them know first, they will not add dairy.

The food was amazing, well-presented & full of flavor even tho they emphasize the health aspect of food. Everything was freshly prepared with minimal processing.

If u happen to stop by Hue, pls visit An Nhien Garden to rest and enjoy incredible food.

reviews.text:
I’m from Germany, went to many places in Danang and mostly I was fine. This place was horrible - from the moment I entered the Spa, there was no welcoming, no one cared. Many random people walked in and out and talked super loud at the lobby, I was not get paid attention for 5min. Then, they asked me to sit down - no tea or warm welcome just “what massage do you want”. I was already annoyed but gave it a shot since so many reviews were positive. I took 90min massage aroma. I asked the front desk why it’s so loud, because even the people behind the front desk were shouting to another stuff at the entrance about things. I asked if it shouldn’t be relaxing and at least the staff should try to be quiet. She just smiled and continued with my booking. The massage itself was ok, nothing special. However, the therapist had middle long nails so it scratched me a lot. Also she seemed to have a flu as she was sniffling with her nose all the time. Afterwards she asked me for a tip which I gave her unwillingly. I left the spa without any beverage, tea or snack.

The service was very disappointing and many “guests” came in and out like it was a Basar.

Paid in the end with tip 700.000 dong - safe your money and go somewhere else where people get greeted, service is welcoming and ambience is quite and chill.

reviews.text:
This was my second visit to this massage spa, and once again, it was an absolutely exceptional experience.

This time, I booked a 2 hour deep tissue massage, as I was looking for a firmer, more intense treatment. It was exactly what I wanted. My therapist was incredibly skilled, applying just the right amount of pressure while remaining gentle and caring throughout the entire session.

What impressed me the most was how attentive she was. She regularly checked to make sure the pressure was comfortable and that I was feeling okay, which made me feel completely at ease. Her professionalism, kindness, and genuine care made this one of the best massages I've ever had.

After two hours, I walked out feeling lighter, deeply relaxed, and completely at peace as if I was floating on a cloud. It was an unforgettable experience.

I also want to thank the entire staff for their warm welcome and kindness. Everyone is so friendly and makes you feel comfortable from the moment you arrive.

If you're in Da Nang, do yourself a favor and visit this place. I can't recommend it highly enough. I'll definitely be coming back again, and again and again ! 😅

Ride the legendary Hai Van Pass by electric motorbike – from only 450,000 VND.

Looking for an unforgettable way to travel from Hue to Da Nang or Hoi An?

Found The Motorbike Station through Google Maps and decided to visit in person to check the bikes and choose the right one. I didn't have a driver's license with me, so the staff immediately recommended an electric scooter — honest advice, not trying to push something I didn't need.
I chose the VinFast and it turned out to be a great bike. Very smooth and quiet, perfect for getting around Da Nang. The best part is the swappable battery — no waiting hours at a power outlet, just swap it for a full one in a couple of minutes and keep riding. No range anxiety at all.
Prices are very fair — no hidden fees, great value for the quality and service. The staff was friendly, the process was quick and transparent, and the shop is open until 22:00 which is super convenient.
I'll 100% rent from them again next year! Highly recommended, especially if you don't have a license or want to try an electric scooter.

reviews.text:
Great service and friendly family business. Rented a 50cc for 5 days and it was a brand new motorbike with less than 1000km on it. Drove to Hoi An and Hue with it and the ride was very smooth. Everything worked perfectly - it was a little slow going up the hills like Hoi Van Pass, but it was a good speed for going around the curves. They also facilited luggage transfers from Da Nang to Hoi An to Hue and back to Da Nang - very easy pickup/delivery.

A word of warning - if you drive to Hoi An or Hue, avoid the main roads because trucks and buses are flying past you and kicking up dust/rocks. Take the scenic drives around the lakes and sea instead.

They also accept card payment with 3% extra charge, which is fine, but there is a 1M VND deposit, which is returned in cash so plan accordingly if you are leaving Vietnam soon after.

A couple minor issues - since it was a new motorbike, there was no license plate and gas was 33% full. It would be good to rent out the bike with a full tank and have it returned as a full tank.

If you’re looking for a truly authentic Vietnamese experience and want to get away from the usual tourist trail, I can’t recommend an Easy Rider tour with Tien Le highly enough!
From my very first contact with Tien, he was friendly, helpful and genuinely interested in creating a day that I would enjoy. He customised the trip for me, including pick-up from my hotel in Da Nang and what followed was an unforgettable 80km round trip through some of the most spectacular scenery in Vietnam.
Riding over the Hai Van Pass to Lang Co Bay was absolutely breathtaking. The views were incredible, and stopping for a fresh seafood lunch right on the beach was a real highlight.
What made the day even more special was Tien himself. He has an amazing knowledge of Vietnamese history and culture, and the stories he shared along the way really brought the places we visited to life. It felt much more personal than simply being taken from one tourist attraction to another.
Another highlight was stopping at Mo Stream near Lang Co Bay, where I had the wonderful experience of swimming with the locals in the clear, refreshing water. We also visited the beautiful Lap An Lagoon, with its spectacular mountain and coastal scenery. Both stops gave me a wonderful glimpse of the more authentic, less-touristy side of Vietnam.
The combination of stunning scenery, local culture, fascinating history, great food and Tien’s warm personality and excellent English made this a genuinely memorable day.
If you’re visiting Da Nang and want to see a different side of Vietnam, book an Easy Rider tour with Tien, as an experienced motorbike driver I never once felt unsafe. It was one of the highlights of my trip, and an experience I’ll remember for a long time!

I had a fantastic full-day ride with Easy Rider Da Nang and truly enjoyed every moment of the journey.

The route was very well designed—starting from the coastline of Da Nang, up through the scenic Sơn Trà Peninsula (Monkey Mountain), across the breathtaking Hải Vân Pass, and continuing to the peaceful Lăng Cô Bay. We ended with a refreshing stop at Mơ Spring, which was a perfect way to relax after the ride.

What made the experience stand out was the guide, Thiện. He was friendly, safe, and very attentive throughout the day. Riding as a passenger behind the guide felt comfortable and secure, even on the mountain roads. The pace was well managed—not rushed, with enough stops to enjoy the views and take photos.
His English is good and communication was smooth overall, though there is still room for improvement to reach a more polished guiding standard.

From an experience point of view, this is more than just transportation—it’s a proper local journey. You feel the landscape, the wind, and the transition from city to countryside in a very authentic way.

For anyone visiting Da Nang and looking for something beyond the standard tour, I would definitely recommend this experience. It offers great value, strong local insight, and a memorable way to explore central Vietnam.

Thank you again to Thiện and the team for a wonderful day.

What Parents Should Know Before Booking a Yacht Charter in Da Nang
Planning a Yacht Charter Da Nang with Children requires careful consideration of safety, comfort, and family-friendly services. To ensure an enjoyable experience, parents should review important booking details and choose a yacht that matches their children’s ages, interests, and individual needs.

Before making a reservation, families should consider the following factors:

Children’s Ages: Confirm age restrictions and whether the yacht is suitable for infants, toddlers, or older children.
Group Size: Check passenger capacity and available space to ensure everyone can travel comfortably.
Trip Duration: Choose a suitable schedule based on children’s energy levels and daily routines.
Yacht Facilities: Ask about shaded seating, restrooms, comfortable spaces, and other family-friendly amenities.

Yacht Safety Da Nang is an essential consideration for travelers planning to explore the city’s beautiful coastline aboard a private yacht or shared cruise. Before departure, understanding onboard safety procedures, life jacket requirements, weather conditions, and crew instructions can help guests feel more confident and prepared. Whether you are traveling with family, friends, or joining a yacht experience for the first time, knowing what to expect is important for a comfortable and enjoyable journey. In this guide, Da Nang Yachts shares key safety considerations, pre-departure preparations, and practical tips to help travelers enjoy their yacht adventure in Da Nang with greater confidence and peace of mind. 

Safety Rules and Equipment to Check Before Departure
Understanding Yacht Safety Da Nang is essential for travelers planning a comfortable and enjoyable journey at sea. Before boarding, guests should become familiar with the yacht’s safety arrangements, available equipment, and basic operating rules.

Yacht Safety Da Nang
Yacht Safety Da Nang
Essential Safety Equipment on a Yacht
Safety equipment plays an important role in protecting passengers during unexpected situations. Before departure, guests should pay attention to the following:

Life Jackets: Confirm that appropriately sized life jackets are available for adults and children.
Lifebuoys: Identify where emergency flotation devices are located.

Can You Charter a Yacht in Da Nang During the Rainy Season?
Yes, yacht charters may operate during Da Nang’s rainy season when weather conditions are safe and the planned route is suitable for sailing.

A Da Nang yacht charter rainy season booking is not automatically unavailable between September and December. Some days bring prolonged rainfall, while others include dry periods suitable for outdoor activities.

The most important factor is the difference between rainy weather and unsafe sailing conditions.

Light rain may not prevent a yacht from operating. However, strong winds, rough water, thunderstorms, poor visibility, or navigation restrictions can make departure unsafe.

When Can Yacht Charters Still Operate?
A yacht experience may proceed when:

Wind conditions: Wind speed and gusts remain within safe operating limits.
Water conditions: Waves and currents are suitable for the vessel and route.
Visibility: The crew can navigate safely.
Weather warnings: No relevant storm warnings or restrictions prevent departure.
Captain’s assessment: The captain confirms that conditions are appropriate.
For travelers considering a Da Nang yacht charter rainy season experience, a relatively dry morning or afternoon may offer a suitable sailing opportunity.

However, favorable weather forecasts do not guarantee departure. Conditions can change, and safety assessments must reflect the actual situation.

The oldest temple in Da Nang, Tam Thai Temple was built around 1630 by monk Hung Lien, who came from China as a monk during the late Le Dynasty.
Among the legends surrounding Tam Thai Temple, the most frequently mentioned is the story of Emperor Nguyen Anh. While being pursued by the Tay Son army, Emperor Nguyen Anh fled to an island off the East Sea.
After a while, he returned and chose Ngu Hanh Son Mountain as his refuge, praying to Buddha that if he could defeat the Tay Son army, he would definitely restore this temple. After ascending to the throne, he ordered Emperor Minh Mang to restore the temple on his own site.
Later, in 1825, during the reign of Emperor Minh Mang, the temple was restored.
This ancient temple is over 400 years old and has unique and ancient architecture.
It is an ideal place to worship and enjoy the beautiful scenery at the temple.
Especially in the morning, the silence and piety will be more intense.

reviews.text: With so many cruise options to choose from, it was difficult to choose and imagine what to expect. However 7 star cruises were great! Contacted them via whatsapp a couple of days before for booking but wanted to pay on the day at the ticket booth which was fine. Lining up system at 8 pm was pretty organised given the large crowds that gather on the weekends for the dragon bridge fire show. Free fruit and bottled water for everyone on the cruise. They have some traditional dancing for entertainment while waiting to leave, then a breezy cruise arcorss the river. The lights and other boats, along with lit up buildings looks so cool. The boat hangs around the dragon bridge so people can watch it fairly close. Good views regardless of seating on the boat because you can move around or come up to the front. Cons: extremely loud music!!! My toddler covered her ears most of the time. It ruined the fire show vibe too as an English wedding song was playing during the show..not related at all?! We actually watch the fire show by the banks of the river, on the ground, the weekend before and prefer that over the boat ride to view it. Would still recommend a cruise ride but not necessarily on the weekend at the fire show slot (8pm), perhaps it would have been quieter with less crowds.

I bought tickets for my wife and me. We made sure that we were back at the line with plenty of time to get on board and get the seats that we wanted. There was no reserved seating. Seats were first come first served when we got in line to board. We were even back to the boat 15 minutes before we had to be. We got on the boat got the seat we wanted. Then one of the staff came and moved us because we were told the person who wanted that seat we were in paid for his ticket before we did, but didn’t get in line in time. By the time that was done, the whole rest of the boat was full and we couldn’t get a good seat at all. In fact, we could not get a seat together. Staff did not seem to care. My speculation is the person who got my seat, tipped the staff so he could get the seat that I properly waited to get. Of course, this was a very bad experience for me. However, the cruise itself was OK and worth the very low cost.

I especially loved the bridge over the pond and the lantern decorations — every corner feels carefully designed and incredibly photogenic while still keeping the spiritual and tranquil vibe of the temple.

It's a pity I didn't see this place in fine weather, but even the dismal weather today didn't determine many Vietnamese ladies visiting this place in their traditional costums for photo shoots. If fine to take photos in the grounds but not inside the Temple which houses a number of shrines. The pools in the grounds have fish, eels and even terapins swimming around. reviews.text:
The building architecture design is nice.

The interior part of the building was also nicely designed. We enjoyed the flow of the museum very much. The historical & cultural as well as the story of Da Nang was very well presented.

We enjoyed the tour in this museum. This is a very well kept and informative museum. Good.

It is nice, clean, and modern. We bought our tickets in advance online via Klook, specifically the option that included the audio guide, and the process was smooth. They provided a dedicated phone and headphones for the tour, which made exploring the exhibits super easy and immersive. Everything was well-organized and all good. Highly recommend visiting if you are in Da Nang!

Proper little history stroll  and you can tell they actually gave yhoughts about the design. From the moment you step in, everything’s laid out in a neat historic timeline: artefacts, stories, the whole lot marching along in order. The place itself is spotless, the entry fee won’t make your wallet cry, and on hotweather of a Da Nang day it’s pure genius duck into the aircon, linger over the history, and pretend the heat outside doesn’t exist.
Very nice museum about Da Na city history. Beautiful building and great displays. Takes 2 to 3 hours to complete without audio guide. Price was 50k /pax without audio guide.

Quick cultural stop before flying back home! We spent about 30 minutes exploring the Da Nang Museum after a relaxing 23-minute walk from our hotel.

The museum was clean, organized, and a nice way to learn more about Da Nang’s history, culture, and military past before ending our trip. Even with limited time, we still enjoyed seeing the exhibits and artifacts that gave us a deeper appreciation of the city. Admission is d 50,000 or about $1.60 per person.

Visiting Da Nang Museum is a new chapter of museum architecture and exhibition display in quality, design and arrangement in Vietnam. Similar improvements and developments are seen at the new military museum in Hanoi!
In Danang the contemporary architecture combines gently the old municipal villas with a modern annex that offers spacious rooms for the exhibition. The alignment of exhibition from colonial times, then American war till traditional ceramic and provincial minority cultures respects the artifacts and provide information mostly bilingual in Vietnamese and English. I would recommend that the video presentations have bilingual subtitles as well. Besides that visitors get a good insight about the Danang area and history. I personally find a more reflective information about the four wars that fought Vietnam for independence very interesting (against French, American, China and Cambodia). That would sum up that history background and provides with information that kept Vietnam in warfare for 40 years from that to recover the country is still working on. Finally, the museum is a great asset for the city! Congrats and kudos!

After the ticket counter you have to scan the ticket barcode to enter. The exhibits start from the local enviroment,geology, ecology and move in a more or less chronological sense from prehistory to the american war. There are interactive displays and the lighting is modern and aesthetic. I also like that they devote a section to the victims of war and agent orange. The way the halls are organised are a lil bit twisty turny, but thats alright. Definately worth a visit.

Visited on 20 May afternoon. Spent about 1 hour 10mins during my trip. There were quite a few locals when I visited. The entrance fee is 50k vnd, while the audio guide which I did not rent is 70k vnd.

There is a small coffee stall and souvenir shop at the entrance of the museum.

title: Da Nang Museum of Cham Sculpture
description: Compact museum displaying a collection of sculptures & cultural items like costumes & instruments.
ownerDescription:
Ranked as one of the first-class museums of the country, with its harmonious and modern displays, the Da Nang Museum of Cham Sculpture is a must-see destination for visitors wishing to discover the culture and heritage of Central Viet Nam.
Visitors will have the opportunity to contemplate more than 400 artifacts on display, including National Treasures and others representing the masterpieces of Champa sculpture in ten centuries (from 5th to 15th). Grounded in various themes from fertility symbols, deities, mythical animals and architectural decoration from the Hindu and Buddhist, they express the features of cultural and religious values of the Champa people over many generations.

reviews.text:
A spectacular experience in the heart of Da Nang. This museum houses the world's largest collection of Cham artifacts, dating from the 5th to the 15th centuries. The intricately carved sandstone sculptures, Hindu deities, and mythical beasts are breathtakingly detailed.

The ancient art and historical stone carvings on display are absolutely incredible. The museum is deeply organized by excavation sites like My Son and Tra Kieu. It is well worth the 60,000 VND entrance fee.

Highlights: The Tra Kieu Pedestal and the recognized National Treasures.

Architecture: Beautiful French-colonial style building designed in 1915 with lovely open courtyards.

It was a hot day when I decided to visit the Da Nang Cham Sculpture Museum. I had planned to visit several other points of interest afterward.

It turned out to be a very ambitious plan 🤭. The museum was much larger than I expected. I ended up spending an hour and a half there.

You could easily spend an entire day immersing yourself in its art. It offers a wide variety of exhibits, including sculptures, handmade crafts, textiles, and visual art from different cities across the country.

By the end, I was exhausted 😆. The third floor doesn’t have air conditioning. I think that’s intentional, perhaps to help preserve the materials.

When I first arrived, there were only three visitors: a Japanese girl, a white guy, and me. We kind of followed the same route through the museum. About an hour later, there must have been more than 100 people there.

There was, I should mention, a special quality about this place. It felt atmospheric, surreal, and almost otherworldly. After spending some time there, I felt as though I had become a part of it.

To enter the museum, you must buy an entrance ticket (60,000 VND, buy on the spot or buy online). Show the QR code for the entrance ticket as many times as you buy, if you buy online. There are 2 floors. When we were there, the 1st floor was quite cold, the 2nd floor was quite hot (the AC might be broken). Overall, it was quite fun to come here with children, seeing statues, clothes, equipment, books from hundreds of years ago. The toilets here are clean. There is a souvenir shop near the museum exit.

Visited on 23 May afternoon. Entrance ticket is 50k vnd. There are a few portable aircons, which helps to cool down the temperature. Quite a few security guards inside, who probably there to remind tourists not to touch the exhibits.

There is a small coffee place and souvenir shop inside the museum as well.

I visited the Da Nang Museum of Cham Sculpture on a weekend, and the experience was exceptional. 🏛️ The exhibits, including an ancient cart and intricate carvings, were beautifully preserved and highly informative. 🏺 I encountered no wait time upon arrival, which allowed for immediate immersion into the rich cultural displays. The museum offers a profound journey through Cham history and artistry.

The Da Nang Museum of Cham Sculpture is a great place to learn more about Cham culture. The Cham Kingdom was an ancient Hindu and Buddhist kingdom that was eventually weakened and integrated into Vietnam.

Entrance tickets are available on many travel platforms, and even via Google Maps. The price was great value for money. Visitors are mostly locals, although I did bump into a few expats during my visit.

The museum's main entrance faces the main road, close to Dragon Bridge. The building itself is an antique structure—I understand it was built by the French nearly a century ago. Therefore, it does not have air conditioning, which made it very hot during summer. Arriving early to avoid the heat is always advisable.

By logging into the museum’s Wi-Fi and going to their website, you can access the audio guide, which provides tremendous help in understanding the exhibits. Unfortunately, it was very difficult to log into the Wi-Fi, and I couldn't find the password either. Some locals helped me, but then I got a 403 Access Denied message because I had a VPN active on my phone. It took nearly 30 minutes to access the audio system, with the help of Gemini. In any event, there are guided tours as well.

The exhibits are amazing. One can see that the Cham Kingdom was deeply influenced by Hinduism and Buddhism. The exhibits include a lot of Buddha sculptures and various Hindu gods. The saddest thing to me was that many exhibits are heavily damaged, probably due to past changes in power. This phenomenon is not uncommon, especially in China.

There is a small cafe stall inside the museum. Alternatively, there is a nearby McDonald's, where I just refuelled with an iced coffee and an ice cream after the visit at a very reasonable price and rested for a couple of hours before moving on to the next spot.

One of the most impressive museums in Da Nang and truly one of the best museums I have visited anywhere. The collection of Cham sculptures and temple elements feels so significant that the museum itself reminds me of a UNESCO heritage site.

The staff here are incredibly kind and passionate. When I told them how interested I was in Cham culture, they even found a book in Russian and helped me learn more about the history and mythology of the Cham civilization. That level of care made the visit very special.

The exhibition is beautifully organized. As you walk through the halls you can see how the space is structured almost like a spiritual journey — with guardian figures such as Yakshas and Dvarapalas watching over the halls with the deities. Deeper inside, you encounter what feel like real temple remains and architectural fragments, reminiscent of places like Angkor Wat.

The museum preserves such a powerful sense of history that you can spend a long time quietly observing each sculpture. I spent almost an entire day here and learned so much.

The only thing I would suggest is adding a little more information about the early formation of the Cham dynasty, especially in the first hall where the map is displayed. A short article or QR code with additional historical context could make the experience even richer for visitors.

Thank you for preserving this beautiful and important culture and sharing it with the world. This museum is absolutely a must-visit in Da Nang.

Tip for visitors: plan at least 2–3 hours for this museum. If you are interested in history, mythology, or archaeology, you could easily spend half a day here.

Highly recommend visiting in the morning when it is quieter — it gives you time to really appreciate the sculptures and the atmosphere of the museum.

A really fabulous museum with very well preserved piece from the surrounding area. Brilliant explanations and clear signage. The photographs throughout really help to tell the stories of the items seen. Air con throughout. Good toilets and cafe is required. Really worth the visit!
