We bought some fresh seafood from the restaurant and asked them to prepare it for us. The restaurant prepared the dish and brought it out to us. Suddenly, while we were eating, a staff member (a thin woman with a gaunt face) came out and said this wasn't our table and asked us to move to another table. We agreed, but she spoke very rudely, saying we sat there without asking anyone. I explained that we had already told them we were tour guide Phuc's group, but we didn't see anyone guiding us, and now they were blaming us. Anyway, I just wanted to keep the peace and only asked for food for the children to eat. But no, the restaurant staff made us wait for over an hour, until 1 PM, while other groups who arrived later got to eat first. After our tour guide returned, they complained that we were seated in the wrong place and had an unpleasant attitude (this was relayed by the tour guide).
It's unacceptable for service staff to have such a petty and resentful attitude towards customers. I wonder if the manager or owner of the restaurant is aware of this? But if the owner reads this review, please retrain your staff. In this day and age, you can tell immediately whether a service is good or not. Even if the restaurant caters to tour groups, it's not a monopoly on the island. If the service isn't good, customers can book in advance to avoid the restaurant.

reviews.text:
What a fantastic experience from start to finish! We began with a visit to the local market before heading out for the coconut boat ride. I paid extra for the spinning experience and it was absolutely worth it! We even had an impromptu crab fishing lesson, which was such a fun surprise.

Back at Mimi’s house, everything was so well organised. The recipes were explained clearly (and sent later that day), all the ingredients were prepared, and there were lots of thoughtful little extras along the way that didn’t go unnoticed (you’ll just have to book it to find out what they are! 😝).

We left with extremely full bellies. My favourites were definitely the spring rolls and the papaya salad—I can’t wait to make them again at home.

Thank you for such a warm, welcoming and memorable day. If you’re looking for an authentic, fun and delicious cooking class in Hoi An, I couldn’t recommend this experience more!

Such a fun experience!!! We started with the market which was insightful to know what goes into all the delicious food we cooked! We then got taken to the coconut boats and had an amazing time singing,spinning and learning Vietnamese with our guide. Finally the cooking class itself was amazing and we made some delicious food!! We ate it all together at the end and it was so lovely to try some new dishes. I will definitely be making them at home and definitely recommend mimis cooking class if you’re in hoi an.

Had an incredible morning with Mimis Cooking Class! Very easy to book and really well organised. Bonus that we were picked up from our accommodation and had a trip around the markets to try local produce! Coconut boats were lots of fun and our guy was brilliant (Go England!!) The cooking class was great, lots of new foods to try and a variety of skills learnt. Overall, great value for money, very engaging and would highly recommended. Thanks again to the Mimis team! All the best

We did the afternoon cooking class today and absolutely loved it! The food was delicious and we were taught so well how to make everything. A lovely touch was getting the recipes after also so you can save them for home ( you will want to make them again they were so good!)

Everyone was very friendly and helpful! 100% recommend :)

My wife and I did Mimis cooking class a few weeks ago and it was amazing!
The market tour to get ingredients, to the boat and then the cooking class were all fun and smooth experiences.
At the market we got to visit different vendors, get indepth information about the different local foods they sold and even got to try some fruits and veggies I have never heard of before.
The boats were a riot. We floated down a beautiful scenic areas and then got the option to get spun in the boats like you see on social media. There was music and laughter. My guide even let us fish for crabs and I caught 2! (Don't forget to tip your boat guide. We gave ours 120,000 VND)
Finally the cooking class was relaxing and fun. The people in the class were a good time, the cooking instructions were super easy to understand and the food was DELICIOUS 😋. Don't worry about tracking the recipes, they will send you everything after the class so you can stay in the moment.
They gave us free waters and the class comes with 1 free soft drink with your meal. One of the best experiences during our Vietnam trip.

We had THE BEST experience at Mimi Cooking Class - the whole morning was so much fun, we loved every single minute of all the activities! We laughed our way through the experience and have learnt so much. We are very excited to try & recreate the food when we are home as it tasted so good!! I highly recommend booking this class if you are in Hoi An as you will have the best time!! The experience also includes the coconut boats which was so fun!

Excellent Experience!!!!!! The best cooking class ever!!! With a trip to the market and sailing on a coconut boat and then cooking the best and tastiest Vietnamese food!!!! The place was clean and  good space,  Such a nice and pleasant instructor !!! it was a perfect day!! me and my two boys!! (14,16) Very Recommended for a fun family  experience!!

We had an absolutely unforgettable experience at this Vietnamese cooking class led by Mimi. From the very beginning everything felt authentic and thoughtfully curated. The day started with a visit to a local market where Mimi shared her knowledge about fresh ingredients and Vietnamese cuisine in such an engaging and insightful way and we were even able to taste different local products.

One of the most special moments was the boat ride with her mother who was incredibly kind and warm and added such a personal and heartfelt touch to the entire experience.

Back in the kitchen the cooking itself was amazing. Every dish we prepared was not only delicious but also beautifully presented and Mimi guided us with patience passion and genuine enthusiasm. You can really feel how much she loves what she does.

This was so much more than just a cooking class it was a cultural experience we will always remember. We truly wish Mimi and her family all the best for the future. Thank you for such a wonderful day!

Wandered through the upper French Village zone, taking in the European-style plazas, spires, and castle courtyards.

The Breakdown:

• SCENERY & ARCHITECTURE: Highly detailed mock-European medieval village featuring ornate spires, grand courtyards, cobblestone lanes, and striking marble interiors. Visually impressive for photography, with endless architectural angles spread across shifting terrace elevations.

• VIBE & DENSITY: The central fountain and church squares see high visitor concentration, but stepping into the peripheral side alleys and elevated viewpoints reveals quiet, almost desolate pockets with cool mountain breezes.

• PRACTICAL TIPS: Navigating the uneven stone steps and ramps requires sensible footwear, especially if moisture rolls off the ridges and slicks the paving stones.

Takeaway: An elaborate mountaintop architectural installation offering fantastic photography angles and relaxed alley strolls away from the main transit paths.

I have never visited France or rather any country of Europe, so strolling through this village was a feeling of walking in somewhere in France.

There are many things in here to enjoy, restaurants, beer shop, gaming zone, roller coaster rides etc. Just walk around the vast complex and absorb the vibe and enjoy.

reviews.textTranslated:
A place to admire the entire Son Tra Peninsula in Da Nang. The Son Tra Peninsula is a "precious gem" of Da Nang, considered the city's green lung that regulates the climate. Located about 10km northeast of Da Nang city center, the peninsula has a unique location with three sides bordered by the sea and one side bordered by the city, creating a unique natural forest ecosystem connected to the sea in Vietnam.

Key features of the Son Tra Peninsula:
* Strategic location: Known as the "eye of Indochina" during the resistance war due to its strategic observation role. This peninsula also acts as a natural barrier protecting against wind and storms and regulating the climate for Da Nang.

* Diverse ecosystem: Son Tra is a place where the typical flora and fauna of both North and South Vietnam intersect.

* Vegetation: Nearly 4,000 hectares of forest, with over 1,000 species of higher plants, including many large trees and valuable medicinal plants. In particular, there is a thousand-year-old banyan tree with a large trunk circumference and a massive root system, creating an impressive landscape.

* Wildlife: It is home to more than 366 animal species, including more than 43 rare species listed in the Vietnam Red Book and the International Red List (IUCN). The symbol of Son Tra is the brown-footed langur, a rare primate known as the "queen of primates". In addition, there are many diverse species of insects, birds, and reptiles.

* Marine ecosystem: The coastal waters of Son Tra are also very diverse with more than 100 species of seaweed and beautiful coral reefs, attractive for scuba diving and exploration.

* Nature Reserve: In 1992, the Son Tra forest reserve was officially recognized as the Son Tra Peninsula Nature Reserve. This is the only nature reserve located within the city limits of a major city in Vietnam.

Attractions on Son Tra Peninsula
Son Tra Peninsula offers a variety of experiences for visitors, from exploring nature to visiting spiritual sites:
* Linh Ung Pagoda at Bai But: A large pagoda with a 67m-tall statue of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara facing the East Sea, a famous spiritual tourist destination and a place where visitors can admire the panoramic view of Da Nang city from above.

* Ban Co Peak: The highest point on the peninsula, associated with the legend of the immortal playing chess. From here, you can gaze out over the entire city of Da Nang, the sea, and the majestic mountains.

* Thousand-Year-Old Banyan Tree: One of the highlights of Son Tra, with the ancient and majestic beauty of an "old banyan tree" that has existed for hundreds of years.

* Son Tra Lighthouse (Tien Sa Lighthouse): Built during the French colonial period, it is not only a lighthouse to guide ships but also an ideal check-in spot with a view of the vast blue sea.

* Pristine beaches: But Beach, Tien Sa Beach, Da Den Beach, Nam Beach... all possess unspoiled beauty, clear blue water, suitable for swimming, fishing, and picnicking.

* Bang Cliff: Distinguished by its unique black rock formations, it's an ideal place for sightseeing and photography.

* Tien Sa Port: An important seaport in Da Nang, welcoming many international cruise ships.

* Tien Sa Eco-tourism Area: Offering a blend of nature and modern amenities, with many outdoor activities.

* Oc Peak: The highest point of the peninsula, nearly 700m.

Potential and Challenges
Son Tra Peninsula has great potential for developing eco-tourism, resort tourism, and spiritual and cultural tourism. However, tourism development must go hand in hand with strict conservation efforts to protect the diverse ecosystem and precious natural landscape of Da Nang's "green lung". Managing investment projects and tourism activities to avoid negative environmental impacts is a major challenge that is receiving attention.
reviews.text:
Một nơi để ngắm toàn bộ bán đảo Sơn Trà Đà Nẵng. Bán đảo Sơn Trà là một "viên ngọc quý" của Đà Nẵng, được ví như lá phổi xanh điều hòa khí hậu cho thành phố. Nằm cách trung tâm Đà Nẵng khoảng 10km về phía Đông Bắc, bán đảo này có vị trí độc đáo với ba mặt giáp biển và một mặt giáp đô thị, tạo nên hệ sinh thái rừng tự nhiên gắn liền với biển duy nhất ở Việt Nam.
Đặc điểm nổi bật của Bán đảo Sơn Trà
* Vị trí chiến lược: Được mệnh danh là "mắt thần Đông Dương" thời kháng chiến nhờ vai trò quan sát chiến lược. Bán đảo này cũng đóng vai trò như bức bình phong che chắn gió, bão và điều hòa khí hậu cho Đà Nẵng.
* Hệ sinh thái đa dạng: Sơn Trà là nơi giao thoa giữa hai hệ động thực vật tiêu biểu của hai miền Nam - Bắc Việt Nam.
* Thực vật: Có gần 4.000 ha rừng, với hơn 1.000 loài thực vật bậc cao, trong đó có nhiều cây gỗ lớn và cây thuốc quý. Đặc biệt, có cây đa ngàn năm tuổi với chu vi thân lớn và hệ thống rễ phụ đồ sộ, tạo nên một cảnh quan ấn tượng.
* Động vật: Là nơi sinh sống của hơn 366 loài động vật, trong đó có hơn 43 loài quý hiếm nằm trong Sách Đỏ Việt Nam và Danh Lục Đỏ Quốc Tế (IUCN). Biểu tượng của Sơn Trà chính là Voọc Chà Vá chân nâu, loài linh trưởng quý hiếm được mệnh danh là "nữ hoàng của các loài linh trưởng". Ngoài ra còn có nhiều loài côn trùng, chim, bò sát đa dạng.
* Hệ sinh thái biển: Vùng biển ven bờ Sơn Trà cũng rất đa dạng với hơn 100 loài rong biển và những dải san hô tuyệt đẹp, hấp dẫn cho hoạt động lặn biển khám phá.
* Khu Bảo tồn Thiên nhiên: Năm 1992, khu rừng cấm Sơn Trà chính thức được công nhận là Khu Bảo tồn Thiên nhiên Bán đảo Sơn Trà. Đây là khu bảo tồn thiên nhiên duy nhất nằm trong nội thành một thành phố lớn ở Việt Nam.
Các điểm tham quan hấp dẫn tại Bán đảo Sơn Trà
Bán đảo Sơn Trà mang đến nhiều trải nghiệm đa dạng cho du khách, từ khám phá thiên nhiên đến tham quan các công trình tâm linh:
* Chùa Linh Ứng Bãi Bụt: Ngôi chùa lớn với tượng Phật Quan Âm cao 67m hướng ra biển Đông, là điểm du lịch tâm linh nổi tiếng và là nơi du khách có thể ngắm toàn cảnh thành phố Đà Nẵng từ trên cao.
* Đỉnh Bàn Cờ: Nơi cao nhất trên bán đảo, gắn liền với truyền thuyết tiên ông đánh cờ. Từ đây, bạn có thể phóng tầm mắt bao quát toàn bộ thành phố Đà Nẵng, biển và núi non hùng vĩ.
* Cây đa ngàn năm tuổi: Một trong những điểm nhấn của Sơn Trà với vẻ đẹp cổ kính, kỳ vĩ của một "lão đa" đã tồn tại hàng trăm năm.
* Hải Đăng Sơn Trà (Hải đăng Tiên Sa): Được xây dựng từ thời Pháp thuộc, không chỉ là ngọn hải đăng định hướng cho tàu thuyền mà còn là điểm check-in lý tưởng với tầm nhìn ra biển xanh bao la.
* Các bãi biển hoang sơ: Bãi Bụt, Bãi Tiên Sa, Bãi Đá Đen, Bãi Nam... đều sở hữu vẻ đẹp nguyên sơ, nước trong xanh, phù hợp cho tắm biển, câu cá và dã ngoại.
* Ghềnh Bàng: Nổi bật với những phiến đá đen độc đáo, là nơi lý tưởng để ngắm cảnh và chụp ảnh.
* Cảng Tiên Sa: Cảng biển quan trọng của Đà Nẵng, nơi đón nhiều tàu du lịch quốc tế.
* Khu du lịch sinh thái Tiên Sa: Mang đến sự hòa quyện giữa thiên nhiên và tiện nghi, với nhiều hoạt động ngoài trời.
* Đỉnh Ốc: Điểm cao nhất của bán đảo, gần 700m.
Tiềm năng và thách thức
Bán đảo Sơn Trà có tiềm năng lớn để phát triển du lịch sinh thái, nghỉ dưỡng và văn hóa tâm linh. Tuy nhiên, việc phát triển du lịch cũng cần đi đôi với công tác bảo tồn nghiêm ngặt để bảo vệ hệ sinh thái đa dạng và cảnh quan thiên nhiên quý giá của "lá phổi xanh" Đà Nẵng. Việc quản lý các dự án đầu tư và hoạt động du lịch để tránh tác động tiêu cực đến môi trường là một thách thức lớn đang được quan tâm.

reviews.text: What a beautiful family experience. We attended without a booking when the shop was quiet and the ladies were so friendly, patient and helpful. Our family of 4 (kids 11 and 12) all made a lantern from scratch and were supported and guided along the way. It was a fun, unique experience, and all the staff ensured our lanterns were well made but allowed each of us to create and learn with their support. The kids love that they made their own souvenir. It was certainly one of our favourite Hoi An experiences.

Really friendly. No advance booking required. Really helpful if you’re not that experienced at crafts. A really cool idea and a perfect holiday souvenir or a great gift for friends.
Really enjoyed it; it’s definitely worth a visit!

We had a great morning making lanterns. Range of sizes, shapes and fabrics to choose from. You can opt to cover a pre-made lantern or make one from scratch. Hubby and my 7 year old did the pre-made and my 11 year old and I did from scratch which took longer. It was really busy when we were there but the staff were helpful and fixed any problems we had (ie cutting the string on the lantern a number of times - oops!). If you go during a busy time you will need to be patient.

We are so excited to display our one of a kind handmade souvenirs when we get home. It’s such an adorable activity and a meaningful item to take home - I’d highly recommend.

What a great find! Spent an amazing time with the family this morning making our own lanterns. We had no crafting experience but the owner and staff were so helpful teaching us along the way. Highlight of our trip to Hoi An!

If you’re visiting Hoi An, you absolutely have to experience The Lantern Lady workshop. It is honestly one of the best around. From the moment I arrived, the family made me feel so welcome — they are incredibly accommodating, kind, and genuinely passionate about what they do.

They guide you through every step of the lantern-making process with so much patience and care, making it both fun and easy to follow. I had such an amazing time learning how to make my own lantern from scratch, and being able to choose my own fabrics made the experience even more special. Creating something beautiful with your own hands, guided by such a lovely family, is truly unforgettable.

This isn’t just a workshop — it feels personal, authentic, and heartfelt. Definitely a must-do while you’re here!

We recently visited The Lantern Lady while staying in Hoi A with our 2 kids (ages 8 & 10) and we had such a great time experience! We went very much thinking that it would just be an activity for the kids but we ended up really enjoying it too. We got so much help and support and everyone really enjoyed the whole process. We were given space to take our time but also help when we needed it and it feels so special to have such a meaningful souvenir to bring home. Really glad we found such a great workshop! Thank you!

We went to the lantern lady without a booking and they managed to fit in my partner and I without any problems (Sunday afternoon). We both made our lanterns from the first step of building the frame and the staff carefully helped us at each part. We spent some time there and we are very happy with our lanterns! They are collapsible so we are able to take them with us on our travels. It's a lovely relaxing environment down a side street and the staff are warm and welcoming. I would highly recommend going to Lantern Lady!

With lanterns lighting up every corner of Hoi An, it’s tempting to just buy one and move on, but this experience lets you actually be part of it.

The staff were incredibly attentive and genuinely helpful. If you made a mistake, they didn’t just fix it for you, they showed you how to do it properly, which made the whole thing feel much more authentic. They guided us through each step without hovering, and were friendly the entire time.

You can customise everything - the shape, size, and fabric. You can either work with a pre-made frame or build the frame yourself if you want the full experience. Best part, the lanterns fold down to roughly the size of a drink bottle, so they’re easy to carry around all day or pack in your luggage.

Honestly considering going back for another one.

We started the day being picked up and sent to the market where we met Lai. There, we were introduced to all the wonderful and interesting ingredients that would be used in our cooking class. reviews.textTranslated:
🌊 Cham Island – A Green Corner of Nature and People 🌿

I've had the chance to visit Cham Island many times, and each time I've returned feeling relaxed and refreshed, like being "recharged" amidst pristine nature. It's an ideal place to learn about the island's marine ecosystem – from coral reefs and seagrass beds to unique marine life.

🌱 What I appreciate most is the local people's awareness of environmental protection and ecological conservation. They say no to plastic bags, minimize plastic waste, and constantly remind visitors to maintain cleanliness – something not every tourist destination achieves.

However, regarding the service organization, I think there should be more innovation and professionalism. Almost every tour only stops at: the exhibition area, the freshwater well, and Hai Tang Pagoda – places worth visiting, but which feel repetitive after multiple visits.

🌤 The morning sun was quite strong, and the range of activities wasn't very diverse. If there were more activities like a series of floating platforms on the sea, or a coconut water stand like a small beach bar, it would definitely attract more visitors – especially young people who love taking photos and enjoy fresh, vibrant experiences.

🇻🇳 But regardless, Cu Lao Cham remains an integral part of our homeland – simple, welcoming, and very Vietnamese. If you haven't been there, come once to understand why it's called "the green pearl in the middle of the Central Vietnamese sea."

#CuLaoCham #TravelReview #VietnameseNature #Ecotourism #OnceToLoveMore
reviews.text:
🌊 Cù Lao Chàm – Một góc xanh của thiên nhiên và lòng người 🌿

Đã có dịp đến Cù Lao Chàm nhiều lần, và lần nào cũng mang về cảm giác thư thái, trong lành như được "sạc lại năng lượng" giữa thiên nhiên hoang sơ. Đây là một địa điểm lý tưởng để tìm hiểu về hệ sinh thái biển đảo – từ rạn san hô, cỏ biển đến các loài sinh vật đặc trưng.

🌱 Điều mình đánh giá cao nhất chính là ý thức giữ gìn môi trường và bảo tồn sinh thái của người dân nơi đây. Nói không với túi nilon, hạn chế rác thải nhựa, và luôn nhắc nhở du khách giữ vệ sinh – đó là điều không phải điểm du lịch nào cũng làm được.

Tuy nhiên, về khâu tổ chức phục vụ, mình nghĩ nên có thêm sự đổi mới và chuyên nghiệp hơn. Hầu như tour nào cũng chỉ dừng lại ở: khu trưng bày, giếng nước ngọt, và chùa Hải Tạng – những nơi rất đáng ghé, nhưng nếu đi nhiều lần sẽ thấy lặp lại.

🌤 Buổi sáng tắm biển thì nắng khá gắt, mà hoạt động trải nghiệm lại chưa đa dạng. Giá như có thêm các trò như cầu phao liên hoàn trên biển, hay một quầy nước dừa như một beach bar nhỏ, chắc chắn sẽ hút khách hơn – đặc biệt là các bạn trẻ mê sống ảo và yêu thích năng lượng mới mẻ.

🇻🇳 Nhưng dù sao đi nữa, Cù Lao Chàm vẫn là một phần máu thịt của Tổ quốc – bình dị, gần gũi, và rất Việt Nam. Nếu bạn chưa từng đi, hãy đến một lần, để hiểu vì sao người ta gọi đây là "hòn ngọc xanh giữa biển khơi miền Trung".

reviews.text: Absolutely stunning ficus tree, with branches arching in all directions. Such beauty is rare to see, my eyes have been blessed, and my fingers graced by the touch of this tree.

What an adventure to get here and what a tree!!! Truly the most beautiful tree I’ve ever been to. So worth the effort of navigating landslides monkeys cows rocks shit on the road - it was an experience I will never forget. Would recommend everyone visit this tree.

Till here the road is in good condition. If you continue till the lighthouse you will have 5 scooter challenges to overcome. Sandy road, slalom through rocks, off-road, over rocks and the last challenge we returned because of missing road!

I love all the trees in the world and this is truly the most beautiful and amazing tree out there.
A visit is a Must!
Coming from the fishing village the road is completly blocked by rockfall after this tree (we went 22. January 2024). But the views of the ocean are still amazing.

The island is not avaible for make trip around the island by motorbike. There are landslides at the northern part so you have to return. However the island is small so you can return. The area, at the north part is beautiful and wild with many cliffs. At the south part of the island there are scenic beaches with Christal clear water.

One thing I wish I knew before coming is that most of the east side of the island is not accessible. There are many rock slides that have some roads closed, the roads that are open have many rocks on the road so the driving is dangerous and difficult especially if you are doubling. The road from the main village to the fishing village is in fine condition. I was excited to explore the island but found it difficult to navigate all the rock falls.

reviews.text:
We had such a fantastic experience here and would highly recommend it to anyone visiting Hoi An.

We chose to visit at 1pm, which turned out to be perfect as it was the hottest part of the day. The workshop is fully air-conditioned, with cold drinks available to buy from the fridge, making it a brilliant way to escape the heat while doing something memorable.

We came as a family with our 4-year-old daughter and grandparents, and it was an activity that everyone could enjoy together. The ladies running the workshop were incredibly patient, kind and encouraging, taking the time to demonstrate every step and helping whenever we got stuck without ever making us feel rushed. They were especially wonderful with our daughter, making sure she was involved throughout, guiding her carefully at every stage and ensuring she was progressing and enjoying herself the whole time. It really made the experience feel inclusive for all ages.

There are two workshop options:
• A 45–60 minute session where you decorate a pre-made lantern frame with your chosen fabric.
• A 90-minute session where you build the bamboo lantern frame yourself before covering it with fabric.

There is a huge selection of beautiful fabrics to choose from, so every lantern feels unique.

One of the best features is that the lanterns are designed to collapse flat, so you can easily pack them into your suitcase and take home a beautiful handmade lantern.

This was one of our favourite activities in Hoi An: relaxing, creative, suitable for all ages, and a lovely way to spend a few hours together as a family. If you’re looking for something different from sightseeing, don’t miss this experience!

reviews.text:
If you stay at Little Riverside Hotel, don’t miss the chance to explore the nearby riverbank area — it’s quiet, local, and full of gentle charm.

In the morning, you’ll see locals riding bicycles, vendors setting up, and the soft mist rising from the Thu Bon River. The pace is calm, almost meditative. You can walk along the narrow streets, spot elegant shop signs, and pass by cafés that haven’t opened yet — it feels like Hội An before the crowds.

Tip: Wake up a little early, bring a camera, and just follow the river. No plan needed.

Lucky was such an amazing tour guide with a wealth of information. She was really great at speaking English and carrying a meaningful conversation with us the entire time. She had so much knowledge about the food and local history. We are so grateful to have had Lucky as our tour guide! We were also SO FULL after our tour, so make sure to go on an empty stomach!

Sam Rocks! , Delicious food tour. Egg Coffee and the Banh Mi were my favorite. I found Sam on YouTube and she didn’t disappoint 😎We did the morning tour so we couldn’t dive in to the heavy duty food, and we were still full.

Got the chance to go on this food tour with Sam today. I’m so glad I did. It was just me and her. I can be a little shy but she made me feel comfortable. She is really nice and made sure I was safe while walking in these crazy streets. The food options were great and diverse. Personally my favorite was the chicken and rice (COM GA). And the Sesame soup. I was really impressed buy how much I liked it since I’m not much of a dessert person. I got to meet some of the local workers and joke around with them. Overall great experience. You should totally book this tour! 🩷

We had the best private walking street food tour with our guide, Lucky! We got to try about eight different dishes, and Lucky was able to cater to our needs and allergies of group members. We got to try a range of items including beverages, small plates, main dishes and dessert at high quality local restaurants and road side shops. Her knowledge as a Hoi An local meant she could answer any questions we had! & make sure you go on an empty stomach 😁

Lucky, our tour guide, took us on a fantastic private tour of the streets of Hoi An. She gave us an insightful look into the lives and culture of the people and food of Hoi An. We went to places that we would never have known about without the tour. We didn't want to be a part of a large tour group, so the private tour was perfect for us and at a very reasonable price.
Lucky also gave us tips about places to visit on our own in the days following which were fabulous. Booking Hoi An Street Food Tours is a must when visiting Hoi An! 10/10.
Sam has been a great guide. We were so full at the end of the tour hahahah. But food was delicious and we stopped at some places where we wouldn’t have had as tourists. Thanks again Sam!!!

reviews.text:
I had a wonderful experience on my day trip to Mỹ Sơn Sanctuary. Everything was thoughtfully planned from start to finish. I received clear confirmation and pickup instructions ahead of time, and the driver made the journey feel safe and easy.

Our guide, Hiếu, was knowledgeable, helpful, and genuinely kind. I learned so much about the local culture and the deep history of the area. The sanctuary itself was magnificent, and the local lunch included on the tour was tasty and relaxing.

The group size was just right & not too big with a mix of solo travelers (like me) and pairs. From what I observed, everyone was treated kindly and taken care of. The boat ride down the river through Hoi An’s old town was such a lovely way to end the day before heading back to Da Nang.

I felt safe, inspired, and enriched throughout the entire experience. Highly recommend.

An absolutely fantastic tour of Hoi An with Jackie!
​If you're looking for a guide who is knowledgeable, fun, and truly passionate about the city, you need to book with Jackie. She made the history of Hoi An feel alive and vibrant, not just a series of facts.
​Jackie was incredible at navigating the Old Town efficiently, pointing out all the hidden gems and local secrets we would have missed on our own. She had a fantastic sense of humor and made everyone in our group feel comfortable and engaged. She even took some brilliant photos for us at the best spots!
​I highly recommend Jackie for anyone visiting Hoi An. Five stars all the way—she is a true professional and made this tour the highlight of my trip. Thank you, Jackie!

We booked this tour via Klook last minute and were expecting it to be a group tour, but it turned out to be just me and my friend — which was such a nice surprise. Our tour guide, TingTing, was very welcoming and easy to talk to. She explained all the spots in Hoi An clearly and shared interesting stories that made us appreciate the place even more. The transportation from Da Nang to Hoi An was smooth and convenient too. Overall, it was a comfortable, meaningful, and enjoyable experience. Highly recommended. 🙏✨

This was the perfect tour for anyone wanting a no frills experience of the My Son Sanctuary and temples. Emma was a fantastic guide, with great English and lots of knowledge about the specifics of the temples and their history. The banh mi and coffee on the way back was delicious. I highly recommend going at 5.30am as we did, as I can see how hot it gets out there! Thanks for the great experience.

Absolutely loved this tour, My Son is a must-visit. The temple grounds are so beautiful with the surrounding mountains, the chirping birds, and the awe-inspiring ancient structures. Our tour guide named Toàn was so friendly and informative, and I was fascinated to learn and ask about everything in My Son. Then we were given some of the best Banh Mi I’ve ever had and I got a perfect egg coffee at the tour’s end. Couldn’t recommend more, so fun!

Had an excellent guide, he was able to answer all the questions I had and I left the tour with a notebook full of intricate details about Mi Son and the history of Vietnam pre/post colonisation and pre/post war. He even suggested other experiences to build on my knowledge and I had no questions left by the end of the tour.

My Son Sanctuary was one of the places that pushed me to travel to Vietnam and I was not disappointed. The sanctuary is absolutely divine in itself but Toan was such an amazing guide that he made the experience even better. Interested, passionate and knowledgeable about the place and its history, Toan helped us re-enacting this civilisation from another time. Thank you so much !

The tour was informative and fun. Our guide Mr. Toan taught us a lot about the history and  some fun facts about My Son Sanctuary and the civilization that used to be here. After the tour at My Son, we went to eat bahn mi and drink coffee. Overall, it was good 😊💯

reviews.text: What a beautiful family experience. We attended without a booking when the shop was quiet and the ladies were so friendly, patient and helpful. Our family of 4 (kids 11 and 12) all made a lantern from scratch and were supported and guided along the way. It was a fun, unique experience, and all the staff ensured our lanterns were well made but allowed each of us to create and learn with their support. The kids love that they made their own souvenir. It was certainly one of our favourite Hoi An experiences.

Really friendly. No advance booking required. Really helpful if you’re not that experienced at crafts. A really cool idea and a perfect holiday souvenir or a great gift for friends.
Really enjoyed it; it’s definitely worth a visit!

We had a great morning making lanterns. Range of sizes, shapes and fabrics to choose from. You can opt to cover a pre-made lantern or make one from scratch. Hubby and my 7 year old did the pre-made and my 11 year old and I did from scratch which took longer. It was really busy when we were there but the staff were helpful and fixed any problems we had (ie cutting the string on the lantern a number of times - oops!). If you go during a busy time you will need to be patient.

We are so excited to display our one of a kind handmade souvenirs when we get home. It’s such an adorable activity and a meaningful item to take home - I’d highly recommend.

What a great find! Spent an amazing time with the family this morning making our own lanterns. We had no crafting experience but the owner and staff were so helpful teaching us along the way. Highlight of our trip to Hoi An!

If you’re visiting Hoi An, you absolutely have to experience The Lantern Lady workshop. It is honestly one of the best around. From the moment I arrived, the family made me feel so welcome — they are incredibly accommodating, kind, and genuinely passionate about what they do.

They guide you through every step of the lantern-making process with so much patience and care, making it both fun and easy to follow. I had such an amazing time learning how to make my own lantern from scratch, and being able to choose my own fabrics made the experience even more special. Creating something beautiful with your own hands, guided by such a lovely family, is truly unforgettable.

This isn’t just a workshop — it feels personal, authentic, and heartfelt. Definitely a must-do while you’re here!

We recently visited The Lantern Lady while staying in Hoi A with our 2 kids (ages 8 & 10) and we had such a great time experience! We went very much thinking that it would just be an activity for the kids but we ended up really enjoying it too. We got so much help and support and everyone really enjoyed the whole process. We were given space to take our time but also help when we needed it and it feels so special to have such a meaningful souvenir to bring home. Really glad we found such a great workshop! Thank you!

We went to the lantern lady without a booking and they managed to fit in my partner and I without any problems (Sunday afternoon). We both made our lanterns from the first step of building the frame and the staff carefully helped us at each part. We spent some time there and we are very happy with our lanterns! They are collapsible so we are able to take them with us on our travels. It's a lovely relaxing environment down a side street and the staff are warm and welcoming. I would highly recommend going to Lantern Lady!

With lanterns lighting up every corner of Hoi An, it’s tempting to just buy one and move on, but this experience lets you actually be part of it.

The staff were incredibly attentive and genuinely helpful. If you made a mistake, they didn’t just fix it for you, they showed you how to do it properly, which made the whole thing feel much more authentic. They guided us through each step without hovering, and were friendly the entire time.

You can customise everything - the shape, size, and fabric. You can either work with a pre-made frame or build the frame yourself if you want the full experience. Best part, the lanterns fold down to roughly the size of a drink bottle, so they’re easy to carry around all day or pack in your luggage.

Honestly considering going back for another one.

reviews.text:
We had such a fantastic experience here and would highly recommend it to anyone visiting Hoi An.

We chose to visit at 1pm, which turned out to be perfect as it was the hottest part of the day. The workshop is fully air-conditioned, with cold drinks available to buy from the fridge, making it a brilliant way to escape the heat while doing something memorable.

We came as a family with our 4-year-old daughter and grandparents, and it was an activity that everyone could enjoy together. The ladies running the workshop were incredibly patient, kind and encouraging, taking the time to demonstrate every step and helping whenever we got stuck without ever making us feel rushed. They were especially wonderful with our daughter, making sure she was involved throughout, guiding her carefully at every stage and ensuring she was progressing and enjoying herself the whole time. It really made the experience feel inclusive for all ages.

There are two workshop options:
• A 45–60 minute session where you decorate a pre-made lantern frame with your chosen fabric.
• A 90-minute session where you build the bamboo lantern frame yourself before covering it with fabric.

There is a huge selection of beautiful fabrics to choose from, so every lantern feels unique.

One of the best features is that the lanterns are designed to collapse flat, so you can easily pack them into your suitcase and take home a beautiful handmade lantern.

This was one of our favourite activities in Hoi An: relaxing, creative, suitable for all ages, and a lovely way to spend a few hours together as a family. If you’re looking for something different from sightseeing, don’t miss this experience!

One of the best experiences we had in Hoi An! The cooking class was fun, interactive, and very well organized from beginning to end.

The chef was incredibly kind, patient, and always happy to help whenever we had questions or needed assistance. He made everyone feel comfortable and ensured that we all had a great time.

The food we prepared was absolutely delicious, and the entire experience was enjoyable, educational, and memorable. I highly recommend this cooking class to anyone visiting Hoi An. Definitely a 5-star experience!

We had a fantastic afternoon doing the market tour and cooking class (we had already done a coconut boat ride so opted out of this). Loved the food and being able to cook and then eat. My 7 and 11 year old loved it and it was easy for them to participate. The business is run by a young family and they were really lovely. K, our guide and chef, was lovely and involved the kids in all steps of the cooking process. We cooked and ate so much! Can’t wait to get home and try out the recipes. Would definitely recommend.

Had the most wonderful day. K looked after us so well and his cooking skills & teaching was great.  We made really scrumptious food, had a great coconut boat ride and visit to the food market.  K explained the different varieties of fresh  Vietnamese produce. So glad we did it!

Felt welcomed into this lovely family owned cooking school sharing some of there family recipes with us.
K was an amazing guide taking us around the market showing us where they buy all there groceries, a nice coconut boat ride and finally the cooking class.

If any of you are considering them and you have little kids in your group, I highly recommend her service. She was so kind, patient and caring. We felt very well taken care of throughout the day.

We started the day being picked up and sent to the market where we met Lai. There, we were introduced to all the wonderful and interesting ingredients that would be used in our cooking class. reviews.text:
Onya Bike Tours – A Journey of a Lifetime

Touring Vietnam by motorcycle has been one of the greatest experiences of our lives.

From day one, we were warmly welcomed and thoroughly briefed on what to expect over the next seven days. The presentation was led by our group leader, Minh, along with his mechanic, Phong.

Our group of six riders ranged in age from our mid-30s to our late 60s, with varying levels of riding experience. Minh immediately put everyone at ease, assuring us that each rider would be capable of navigating every stage of the tour, while making it clear that safety was always his number one priority.

During the orientation, we were given a clear overview of each day’s ride while still leaving a few surprises for us to discover along the way. The evening before departure, we were fitted with our riding gear and provided with dry bags, bungee cords, and rain gear.

On the morning of departure, we inspected our motorcycles with the staff before setting off. At the end of every day, the bikes were checked, serviced, and prepared for the next day’s adventure, giving us complete confidence in the equipment.

The true highlight of this journey was Minh’s extensive knowledge of Vietnam’s history. He shared fascinating stories and insights into the country’s struggles, resilience, and remarkable journey to where it is today. Every historical site we visited was followed by an engaging explanation that brought each location to life. His passion for his country was evident and added tremendous value to the experience.

The riding itself was exceptionally well planned. We experienced stunning mountain vistas, winding roads, incredibly twisty sections, and relaxed scenic touring. It truly was a motorcyclist’s dream.

We do have a few suggestions that we believe would make an already excellent tour even better while adding another layer of safety:

* Equip the guides and riders with communication systems. Being connected to the guides—and to each other—would be especially valuable when navigating the busy and often chaotic traffic in the cities. At a minimum, both guides should have communication systems.
* Carry a small supply of miscellaneous repair items, such as visor hardware or basic helmet parts, to deal with minor equipment issues that can arise during a week-long tour.
* Replace some of the rain gear. Although it was worn correctly, several riders still became quite wet during heavy rain.
* Give guides the flexibility to recognize when a particular section of terrain may be beyond the comfort level of some riders and offer an alternate route when appropriate.
* Ensure the lead guide is equipped and trained to act as the initial responder should an emergency occur.

We also want to commend your entire team for the professionalism shown throughout the trip. The hotels were, in general, comfortable and well chosen. Minh consistently selected outstanding restaurants that showcased the unique flavours of each region while offering fresh, healthy, and authentic Vietnamese cuisine. Every meal was memorable.

Thank you to the entire Onya Bike Tours team for an unforgettable adventure.

On behalf of Paul, Gary, Nauris , Lauris, Brian, and Don—thank you for creating memories that will last a lifetime.

Wow what an epic trip. Hawk and his team did a fantastic job - great hotels, lovely food, off the beaten track roads and loads of knowledge about the country and different areas. If you want to tour the real Vietnam look no further and just book - you won’t regret it!!

questionsAndAnswers.question: I want to know, is Hot Stone Massage and Aroma Massage in Hoi An different from Da Nang?

answers.answer:
Hot stone Massage: Combine the traditional massage method and use hot (warm) stones to apply to your body, use in combination with essential oils from lemongrass. Reduced muscle tension, reduced stress and anxiety, better sleep and better mental health.

Aroma Massage: Using natural herbal flavors, wrapped in cloth and rubbing on your body, combined with pure essential oils from lemongrass or coconut, or Vaseline (for sensitive skin). Purify your body and especially your skin. Helps skin look young and full of life. Stimulates blood vessels and increases the volume of red blood cells in the body.

Basically, massage in Hoi An or massage in Da Nang are the same. It only differs by the technique of the massage therapist.

I’ve had massages around the world and the aroma massage is unique to Vietnam. Highly recommend it! The dried herbs are wrapped in a cloth and are kind of “stamped” on your body and moved around in massaging motions. I find it similar but definitely distinct from the hot stone and hot bamboo massages.
Not sure as i did not have one at Da Nang

reviews.text:
Great experience seeing woodcrafting. We spend here about 2 hours doing a small workshop, talking with locals, see woodcrafters at work, visit some shops and drink a coffee near the river.
The area is a bit catered towards tourists, but still felt authentic to me. Especially after talking a bit with some of the people. They are super friendly.

If you want to explore a traditional craft village and learn more about the local culture in Hoi An, Kim Bong Carpentry Village is definitely a destination worth experiencing.
When I came here, I had the chance to learn about the traditional carpentry craft that has been preserved through many generations. What I enjoyed the most was seeing the artisans carve, engrave, and shape wooden products by hand. Each product shows the skill, care, and dedication of the craftsmen. 🪵🔨
The most interesting experience was getting to try making a simple wooden product by myself, feeling how challenging each step was and understanding more about the value of the traditional carpentry craft. It was not only a fun activity but also helped me appreciate more the cultural values preserved in this craft village.
The village is peaceful, rustic, and close to nature, giving a completely different feeling from the busy atmosphere of Hoi An Ancient Town.
It was an experience that was both interesting and meaningful, especially suitable for those who love culture, traditional handicrafts, and want to discover a more peaceful side of Hoi An.

so underrated . the visit was really nice, you get to learn about mat making (chiếu), scent sticks (hương), boat fixing, and carpentry in a single trip. the artists were so friendly,  amazing activities and vibe. highly recommended

A bit commercial gift items but still many authentic craftsmanship items with a higher price tag. There are some workshops for basic and advanced wood carving, the artists are friendly and happy to explain about their work.

nice and quiet village about 10-15 minutes drive from the old city, for just 35,000 vnd you get to walk around the village and see the craftsmen at work as well as the finished artifacts, you also get to experience wood carving a Keychain which you can keep as a souvenir.

We were short of time, so we did not manage to stay for long. However, the experience was still very much worth it.
The pricing is fair, as there are both discounts for young children and the elderly, and even without the discounts, I found that the tickets themselves were a bargain in prices considering how much you can do it with them.
The activities within the village were interesting. Apart from getting to see some beautiful carpentry, you also get to try carpentry yourself FOR FREE and get gifts FOR FREE. Even if you are not interested in creating your own works, I believe it is always a pleasure to watch dedicated artisans show their craft as well.
Overall, very worth it.
The Kim Bong carpentry village was really cool. We started out by learning how houses were built in the past, without metal nails, then went to learn about wood carving.

This island village gives you more authentic experience of Vietnamese country village life and their woodworking art. But of course there are places solely for tourists where you can buy wooden souvenirs for better price and give money straight to people who made them. As a bonus you can make your own little bit of wood with carved letters or anything U want.

reviews.text: Outstanding view point

reviews.textTranslated:
Monkey-Faced Rock – Cham Island
Amidst the endless waves of a thousand years,
A silent rock face gazes at the vast sky,
Like an old monkey contemplating by the dreamy sea,
Listening to the wind tell stories of the primeval world.
The mountain speaks, yet seems to have waited,
Many waves come and go without warning,
The deep eyes of the rock—containing a thousand years of silence,
Watching humanity change like a hazy smoke.
Whoever passes by, please stop for a couple of hours,
To listen to the sea speak in wordless language,
To understand that amidst life's transformations,
There are things that remain still and become eternal.
That rock—is not just silence,
But the soul of the earth, of the blue sky,
Bearing the form of a monkey—and carrying all of human life,
Contemplating amidst the endless waves.
Cham Island—where nature remains,
A gaze turned to stone in the vast ocean,
Asking the rock: "What have you seen?"
The rock does not answer—only smiles at the wind.
reviews.text:

Giữa sóng biếc nghìn năm vỗ miệt mài,
Một khuôn mặt đá lặng nhìn trời rộng,
Tựa con khỉ già trầm tư bên biển mộng,
Nghe gió kể chuyện đời thuở hoang sơ.
Núi không nói, mà như đã đợi chờ,
Bao con sóng đến rồi đi không hẹn,
Mắt đá sâu—chứa nghìn năm lặng lẽ,
Nhìn nhân gian đổi thay tựa khói mờ.
Ai ghé qua, xin dừng bước đôi giờ,
Để nghe biển nói bằng tiếng không lời,
Để hiểu rằng giữa cuộc đời chuyển biến,
Có những điều bất động hóa vĩnh hằng.
Hòn đá kia—đâu chỉ là im lặng,
Mà là hồn của đất, của trời xanh,
Mang dáng khỉ—mà mang cả nhân sinh,
Đang suy ngẫm giữa vô cùng sóng gió.
Cù Lao Chàm—nơi thiên nhiên còn đó,
Một ánh nhìn hóa đá giữa trùng khơi,
Hỏi đá rằng: “Ngươi đã thấy gì rồi?”
Đá không đáp—chỉ mỉm cười với gió.

Oregon State Liquor Tax Stamp, USA – circa 1935

This stamp, part of the Oregon state liquor regulatory system, bears the inscriptions "OREGON LIQUOR" and "LIQUOR CONTROL COMMISSION." The central emblem features the words "THE UNION," surrounded by the text "STATE OF OREGON."

According to specialized catalogs, this square, blue-colored stamp is designated as "LS2" and exists in both perforated and imperforate varieties. It was used for the purpose of regulating liquor within the state of Oregon’s control system.

The number "1859" on the emblem refers to the year Oregon became the 33rd U.S. state—on February 14, 1859—and does not indicate the year the stamp was issued.
미국 오리건 주 주류세 인지 - 1935년경

이 인지는 오리건 주 주류 관리 시스템에 속하며, "OREGON LIQUOR and LIQUOR CONTROL COMMISSION"이라는 문구가 새겨져 있습니다. 중앙의 문양에는 "THE UNION"이라는 글자가 있고, 그 주변을 "STATE OF OREGON"이라고 둘러싸고 있습니다.

전문 분류에 따르면, 이 정사각형 파란색 인지는 LS2 코드로 분류되며, 톱니 모양과 톱니 없는 두 가지 변형이 있습니다. 이 인지는 오리건 주 주류 관리 시스템 내에서 주류 통제를 위해 사용되었습니다.

문양에 있는 숫자 1859는 인지가 발행된 해가 아니라, 오리건 주가 미국의 33번째 주가 된 해인 1859년 2월 14일을 나타냅니다.

TEM BƯU CHÍNH QUÂN SỰ ĐỨC
Ngày phát hành: 24/11/1944.
Feldpost: bưu chính quân sự (military field post).
2 kg: giới hạn trọng lượng 2 kilôgam.
Deutsches Reich:  nước Đức thời kỳ lịch sử trước năm 1945.

Phát hành nhằm cho phép gửi những bộ quần áo mùa đông rất cần thiết từ Đức đến các binh sĩ đang chiến đấu ở Mặt trận phía Đông, nơi họ không được trang bị đầy đủ để chống chọi với mùa đông nước Nga.

Được in đè dòng chữ “FELDPOST 2kg” (bưu chính quân sự – 2 kg).

Tem được in lõm, theo từng tờ gồm 100 tem, tại Xưởng in Nhà nước Berlin. Giấy in không có hình chìm, có răng tem K 14, với bề mặt giấy có gân dọc hoặc nhẵn.

Mặc dù trên tem ghi giới hạn trọng lượng 2 kg, người ta tin rằng những bưu kiện nặng hơn 2 kg vẫn được chấp nhận gửi mà không cần dán thêm tem cước.
GERMAN MILITARY FIELD POST STAMP

Issued: 24 November 1944
- Feldpost: Military field post.
- 2 kg: Maximum stated parcel weight.
- Deutsches Reich: Germany before 1945.
This label allowed essential winter clothing to be sent from Germany to soldiers fighting on the Eastern Front, where many lacked adequate protection against the Russian winter.

It features the overprint “FELDPOST 2kg” and was recess-printed in sheets of 100 at the Berlin State Printing Works. The unwatermarked paper was either vertically ribbed or smooth, with perforation K 14.

COLONIAL POSTAGE STAMPS – A GLIMPSE INTO WORLD HISTORY

This collection features rare antique postage stamps with distinctive gold-bronze embossed designs, reflecting the postal history of various territories and colonies around the world, including the Straits Settlements, India, Australia, Malta, Sudan, and Aden.

Portraits of kings and queens, historical figures, cultural symbols, and characteristic landscapes reveal the political and cultural heritage of different periods, as well as the development of postal systems. Beyond their collectible value, these stamps serve as fascinating visual records of history, artistic design, and cultural exchange between nations.

At CSO Gallery Hoi An, each stamp tells a miniature story of history, connecting the past and present through the unique imprints of the world.

Câu chuyện của CSO Gallery không đơn thuần là câu chuyện về tiền xu, tem bưu chính hay sách Truyện Kiều. Một người sưu tầm. Ba thế giới. Hàng nghìn câu chuyện đang chờ được kể.

CSO Gallery — Where Vietnam’s Stories Come Alive.
The story of CSO Gallery is not merely about coins, postage stamps, or editions of *The Tale of Kieu*. It is the journey of an individual who has spent over 25 years pursuing a passion for collecting, creating a space that bridges three cultural worlds and offers the public an opportunity to explore the history of both Vietnam and humanity.

One collector. Three worlds. Thousands of stories waiting to be told.

CSO Gallery — Where Vietnam’s Stories Come Alive.
L'histoire de la galerie CSO ne se résume pas à des pièces de monnaie, des timbres ou des exemplaires du Conte de Kieú. C'est le parcours d'un homme qui, pendant plus de 25 ans, a cultivé sa passion pour le collectionnisme, créant un lieu de rencontre entre trois univers culturels et offrant au public la possibilité d'explorer l'histoire du Vietnam indissociable de celle de l'humanité.

Un collectionneur. Trois mondes. Des milliers d'histoires à raconter.

Galerie CSO — Là où les histoires du Vietnam prennent vie.

CSO Gallery — From a Collector’s Passion to a Global Cultural Destination

In the historic town of Hoi An, Vietnam, a private collection has grown into a cultural space where history, literature, currency and world postal heritage come together.

CSO Gallery began with a passion for collecting — but collecting was only the beginning.

Over time, individual objects became collections. Collections became research. Research became stories. And those stories became an experience for visitors.

Today, CSO Gallery presents an extensive world of ancient currencies, stamps, Vietnamese cultural heritage and The Tale of Kieu, connecting Vietnam with stories from many countries and periods of history.

The Gallery's journey is rooted in one simple idea:

Collecting → Preserving → Researching → Storytelling → Educating.

Rather than keeping collections hidden away, CSO Gallery seeks to turn them into a living space of knowledge — a place where visitors can see, discover and understand history through authentic objects.

Located in Hoi An, one of Vietnam's best-known cultural destinations, CSO Gallery is now becoming increasingly visible beyond Vietnam.

Its presence extends across international travel platforms and tourism ecosystems, including Marriott, Agoda, Booking.com, Viator, GetYourGuide, Klook, Tripadvisor, Traveloka, Trip.com, KKday and other regional platforms.

Artisans near Hoi An have been handcrafting sleeping mats for generations.

The process begins by gathering reeds, which are then dyed in vibrant colors and laid under the sun for several days before being carefully woven. It is a demanding and delicate craft, requiring patience, precision, and experience passed down through families.

The result is more than a simple object, it is a beautiful expression of Vietnamese craftsmanship and tradition.

Have you ever seen traditional crafts like this in Vietnam?

Visit the Precious Heritage Museum to discover their stories through photography and learn more about Vietnam’s diverse ethnic communities.

📍 26 Phan Boi Chau, Hoi An | Free entrance

For many ethnic groups in Vietnam, indigo dye is still handmade using ancestral techniques. Leaves are harvested, fermented, and transformed into deep natural pigments used to dye traditional clothing by hand.

The marks left on the hands tell part of that story. A sign of craftsmanship, patience, and a living tradition that still survives today.

Visit the Precious Heritage Museum to discover their stories through photography and learn more about Vietnam’s diverse ethnic communities.

reviews.text:
I’ve been to quite a few museums, and most of the time they feel very grand and formal, with all these beautiful pieces displayed with information about where they came from, what they mean, when they were made, etc.

But this little museum in Hoi An felt so different to me.

Everything felt so personal. The clothes, accessories and other pieces weren’t just there as exhibits. They were displayed together with photographs of the actual people and communities they came from, and Réhahn himself had met and photographed many of them during his travels around Vietnam.

Even the descriptions beside the pieces didn’t feel like the usual museum plaques. They felt more like little stories about the people, how he met them, and the places he visited.

I don’t really know how to explain it properly, but walking through the museum almost felt like I was there with him when he met these people. Looking at the photographs, especially their faces and their eyes, somehow made me feel like I had met them too.

Out of all the museums I’ve visited, I don’t think I’ve ever experienced one that felt this intimate and human. I’m honestly not even a very sentimental person, but there were moments walking around where I genuinely felt a little emotional.

Such a small art gallery museum, but probably one of the most memorable ones I’ve visited.

The Réhahn Team

reviews.text: Gorgeous museum that offers an authentic glimpse into Vietnamese culture & history. The museum is completely free to enter, however it is well worth a donation. We spent several hours here and ended up coming back a second time to be able to see it all. The photographer is thoughtful and has clearly given so much back to the ethnic groups represented throughout the museum. There is a coffee shop next door that was great for taking a break and getting a cold drink, as there is no A/C in the museum and it was quite hot.
reviews.responseFromOwnerText:
Thank you so much for your visit Tara

We are honored that you visited not once, but twice! The Precious Heritage project was created to offer visitors a deeper understanding of Vietnam’s ethnic groups, cultures, and traditions, and we are delighted that you found the experience meaningful.

Thank you for your kind words and support.

🌏 Want to keep exploring Vietnam’s cultures? Discover more on our Museum Instagram: @precious_heritage_museum.

reviews.text:
We visited this gallery and it’s absolutely stunning, the photographs are beautiful! The artist Réhahn is a French photographer; he shares his story and his journey, having traveled to meet ethnic tribes throughout Vietnam! We were captivated by his books and decided to buy one, we chose Volume 3!
Since we were limited by the weight of our suitcases, Ngoc, the gallery representative, explained that they could ship it directly to our home for an additional fee, of course but it would be much cheaper than buying it online once we got back to France. She gave us great advice and was so lovely! With the purchase of the book, we could take home 5 postcards, and we had a hard time choosing because they were all so beautiful, so she gave us the 6th one for free!
You’ll also find the museum where replicas and unique clothing from different tribes are on display. A wonderful shop thanks again, Ngoc!
reviews.responseFromOwnerText:
Thank you very much, Sarah, for your thoughtful review.
We’re delighted that you enjoyed both the gallery and the museum, and that Réhahn’s journey through Vietnam’s ethnic groups resonated with you. Choosing Volume 3 to take part of that journey home is a meaningful choice.

We’re also happy to hear that Ngoc could assist you and help make the best decision for shipping and your selection of postcards. Sharing these stories, traditions, and cultural heritage through photography and books is at the heart of the Precious Heritage project.


🌏 Want to keep exploring Vietnam’s cultures? Discover more on our Museum Instagram: @precious_heritage_museum.

reviews.text: Wonderful museum. Showcases a photographer's years of hard work to establish relationship with various ethnic groups across Vietnam. Great documentation and collection of various ethnic fashion, craftsmanship, and tradition.
reviews.responseFromOwnerText:
Thank you for taking the time to share how much the garments and handmade pieces stood out to you. We’re glad you spent time with them in our museum.

The Réhahn Team

title: Cookalocal Hội An Cooking Class & local experiences
ownerDescription:
Experience an authentic local cooking class in Hoi An — where you'll not only learn to cook Vietnamese food but also truly live like a local.

The journey begins at the traditional market, where you'll discover fresh ingredients, distinctive spices, and the genuine rhythm of local life. Then, you'll board a basket boat and navigate through the peaceful mangrove forest — a unique experience of Central Vietnam.

The journey concludes in a cozy little kitchen where you'll prepare traditional dishes yourself under attentive guidance. Each dish carries the flavors of home, simple yet rich, deeply connected to the culture and people of this region.

👉 No fuss, no mass tourism — just authentic, intimate, and memorable experiences.

reviews.text:
Beautiful beach without any daytourists.

The 30.000 vnd fee is a scam of some kind, the locals know it's not real and the sign is only in English. Upon asking the "manager" about his license to prove he was telling the truth, he couldn't show me anything.
You should ask him to give you a receipt with an official stamp before paying, he'll not be able to.
In the end we just walked past him... it's not about the money, it's about being treated like an idiot.
Yes, they provide some old chairs they took from somewhere else, but the beach is dirty all over and I even saw the "manager" leave a big plastic bag behind.,when he went fishing/swimming on the turtle protection beach on the other side of the rocks... no dignity, no respect for nature.
To be honest, I could imagine that the turtle protection zone is maybe including the bigger beach with the palm trees as well.
Great beach with almost no people. It costs 30.000 but it's worth it, as it's clean.

This is a the best beach in the island for only 30k per person in what I think is a closed down resort. There is 2 nice men running it who clear rubbish from the main section of beach, have chairs you can use (no extra cost), ample shade from the palm trees and also have nice dogs who stop the monkeys stealing your stuff.

100% recommend, there is no drinks/food on sale so make sure to bring your own.

Bãi Bắc Beach is located in the grounds of an abandoned resort. The beach itself is quite nice, with plenty of natural shade under the palm trees, making it a pleasant spot to relax.

Unfortunately the area is quite littered and the seawater was murky during our visit. There isn’t much to see for snorkelers either, so I wouldn’t recommend it if you’re looking for marine life.

It’s best to bring your own drinks and snacks, as there is no facilities. Access to the beach is very easy and straightforward, making it a convenient stop if you’re exploring Cham Island.

The beach and the water are polluted by the thousands of boats arriving at the shore every day. Many visitors get drunk on the beach, leaving behind piles of trash, while the bars blast loud music that drowns out what little nature remains.
This island left me genuinely saddened. It is a powerful example of how uncontrolled mass tourism can destroy a place that was once truly beautiful. Shame.

No facilities like showers or chairs. Park on road with the locals and rest under the trees in the shade.

This is the most beautiful island all over the country, for me.  This beach especially is calm with no rushing waves, white sand, and clear blue water, no benches for tourists, all so natural.  Most of all, not crowded. Find a shade under trees if you want to stay longer.  or just lie in the water.

reviews.text:
We made a very early morning visit to one of the most important temples in Hoi An, the Chùa Pháp Bảo, a Mahayana temple. It is the headquarters of Hoi An’s Buddhist Association.

The flowers in the courtyard were exquisite; the elaborate landscaping here (and everywhere) is to celebrate Tet.

It was a lovely and peaceful time to visit. They were only two other people there praying.

This was the first significant stop on our morning walking tour of
Hoi An old town . The Phap Bao Pagoda, is located at 7 Hai Ba Trung Street in Hoi An.

On entering the grounds we were asked to don a light covering over our bare legs as a mark of respect.

The building and beautiful gardens are marvelous. It showcases traditional Vietnamese architecture with intricately carved wooden beams, majestic Buddha statues, and serene, colourful gardens.

The pagoda serves as a focal point for the local Buddhist community.

A lovely peaceful, shady place to escape the hub bub and heat of the town.

Beautiful temple. Lovely big trees in the courtyard and lots of flowers. Lovely free to visit after you have used up your five places on the city pass.

Seemed more serious about wearing no shorts in the temple proper, with more signs than the usual.

I stopped by to take a break from the hot sun. There was a shaded area to sit. There were no restrooms in sight. A sign in the main hall said shorts were not allowed. It didn't feel like a temple. It was just a tourist attraction, lost in the crowds. There were no designated areas to explore, and the sky was blue. Not bad for a short rest. There is a parking fee for motorcycles and bicycles in front. It is 5000 VND. The beach is 10K VND, but it's cheaper here in the city center. Shouldn't it be the other way around?

Chua Phap Bao Pagoda in Vietnam is a Buddhist temple located in the ancient town of Hoi An. The pagoda features traditional Vietnamese architecture with colorful decorations and intricate roof carvings of dragons. The grounds are beautifully landscaped with a variety of vibrant flowers and plants.
A white statue of a Buddha figure can be seen on the right side of the garden. We went here from Da Nang city centre by bus. And then from the bus station we walked some meters to the ancient town of Hoi An.
Nice little retreat from the heat. Provide free clothes to cover up so that you can go into the building. Takes 5-10 minutes to get around, worth a visit 🙂

Beautiful simple Buddhist Temple. Only stayed couple minutes as someone was praying at the time. Beautifully laid odd, lots of gold & red and beautiful curtains covering the exterior, instead of doors.
Recommend a look even just outside.

Beautiful Buddhist temple pagoda in the ancient town of Hoi an. We went walking from our hotel Golden holiday hotel and spa. It’s a beautiful town. And you are not allowed to wear short dresses or shorts. They have clothes outside that you can use to cover your knee and shoulders. Closes after 4.30 pm. You need to buy entrance tickets for 3-4 attractions just before the pagoda. There is a booth.
Phap Bao Temple, which you can find on Phan Chu Trinh street. It’s a big temple. Some interesting read. Calm and serene. Not many people.

It was a great experience. And my kind of class - easy to follow, not too taxing ending with a yummy shared lunch. I look forward to making the dishes when I get home.
Highly recommend on a visit to Hoi An.

This experience was the one of the highlights of our trip to Hoi An.

The chef-proprietor personally picked us up from our hotel and whisked us away to his restaurant where we were provided bikes.

After a relaxing and picturesque ride we reached the Tran Que Vegetable Village and the chef took us around the fields showing us all the herbs and how to identify them. Eating herbs straight off the farm was an absolutely delightful experience.

After that we cycled back to a market where one can purchase fresh vegetables. The chef helped us cool down with a great fruit smoothie and fabulous Hoi An pancake. Knowing that this was 100% vegetarian made the experience that much better.

Once cooled off we went around the market identifying different sellers and vegetables.

Post this, it was time for the cooking to begin which meant another short ride to the main restaurant.

It is an extremely nice setting in which to learn how to make 6 different dishes and some base sauces. One of the best aspects was that the chef not only made it seem easy but made you experience it as well. Which increases your confidence to replicate this for when you return back home.

After cooking we sat down to eat and all of it was incredible.

Highly recommend this experience.

Fantastic experience for all food lovers (not just vegetarians). Morning  started with an easy bike ride to an organic vegetable and herb farm. Then we rode through rice paddies to a local market to get the vegetables and herbs for the cooking class while enjoying street food snacks and drinks. The class wS outstanding, easy to follow, lots of useful tips and great fun. The best part? Sitting down for a shared lunch with 6 delicious dishes we had just created. Great value at 900k VND

This was one of the highlights of our stay in Hoi An. We had a wonderful experience, as it's more than just a cooking class. Our private tour started with a visit to a gorgeous organic vegetable farm where we got explanations about the herbs used in Vietnamese cooking. Normally this part is done by bike, but as we could not do this, the chef picked us up from our hotel with his car and drove us back and forth to the farm. After that we made a trip to a local market, where we got to try some local snacks and buy fresh ingredients for the class. Then we had the cooking class with delicious food, which we got to eat at the end of the class. We prepared 6 dishes. We learnt so much and will definitely be using the recipes, which the chef sent us by email, to cook at home! Definitely recommend this cooking class tour!!

I came for a class with my girlfriend and we had a great time. It was just the two of us in the class so it was easy to feel involved and relax. The tour in the morning was lots of fun and the food of course tasted great. We recieved copies of the recipe by email and I can't wait to try them when we get home.

It's also one of the first activities I've taken part in that didn't pressure us to buy more / write reviews etc so thank you for that :)

The cooking class is really amazing! Visiting the vegetable garden and the local market with the bicycle was lots of fun. After that we learned a lot about the vietnamese kitchen and how to prepare six simple but so delicious dishes with ingredients that you can also find at home, which is great. We also got the recipes and we’re looking forward to cook the meals at home. Thanks a lot for this wonderful experience!
Great teacher and amazing recipes! It’s a great experience, highly recommend

reviews.text:
Absolutely stunning viewpoint overlooking the entire main village on Cham Island!
This spot is pure magic - you get a panoramic view of the whole village, the harbor, and the surrounding turquoise waters. Perfect for photos, especially at sunset or golden hour. The scenery feels wild and untouched, exactly why I love exploring Cham Island.

Pro tip: The road leading up here is quite steep and narrow with some sharp turns, so ride carefully on your scooter (especially if it's raining or you're not used to Vietnamese mountain roads). Take it slow, use low gear, and enjoy the ride - it's worth every bit of effort.

Highly recommend detouring here if you're on the island. One of the best free viewpoints around. Bring water and your camera!

reviews.text: We took the tour from Da Nang to Hoi an. It was so much fun. We got picked up at our hotel and dropped off at our next hotel in Hoi an. I would definitely recommend doing this tour to anyone who wants a fun way for going from A to B or if you just want to go sightseeing.

An absolute bucket list experience – I had a headache from smiling so much!
​If you are traveling between Hue and Hoi An, do yourself a massive favor and forget the bus or train. Booking a trip with the Lee Family Riders was hands down one of the best things we’ve ever done.
​We actually just randomly bumped into them while we were walking around the Citadel in Hue. Honestly, when they first pitched it to us, it felt a bit too good to be true. We were naturally pretty skeptical about a random happening like that on the street, but we decided to take the chance—and man, did it pay off!
​I opted to ride my own bike, while my wife sat passenger, and the setup was absolutely perfect for both of us. The coastal and mountain roads are spectacular, but what makes this tour so stress-free is how organized they are. You don’t have to worry about a thing—they take your big suitcases and transport them safely ahead of you, so you're completely free to just enjoy the freedom of the road.
​Also, quick tip for booking: they ask for payment via PayPal, which can sometimes make you hesitate with independent tours, but don't be put off by it at all. It is 100% legit.
​Cruising over the Hai Van Pass with the wind in your face and those insane coastal views is something we will never forget. The guides are absolute legends—incredibly safe, they know the roads like the back of their hand, and they keep the energy high the entire day. By the time we rolled into Hoi An, my face genuinely ached because I had a headache from smiling so much.
​An absolute 11/10 experience. If you get the chance, just do it!

We rode on the back of the motorbikes and felt incredibly safe the entire time. The drivers are highly skilled, professional and amazing guides who love sharing their culture.
Cruising over the spectacular Hai Van Pass was an unforgettable experience. The stops were also perfectly timed, including a refreshing swim at the waterfall, exploring the Marble Mountains and a delicious local lunch.
To top it off, they took seamless care of our heavy luggage, delivering it safely to our next hotel ahead of us. With unlimited cold drinks and genuine hospitality, they truly make you feel like friends. Highly recommended!

We really enjoyed how we were able to get back to our hotel to freshen up before heading back out for dinner. My 69 year old mum was well catered for throughout the day. We’d already visited the Marble Mountains on our last trip, so our driver changed the itinerary for us. We rode through the Hai Van Pass, stopped for a swim and lunch, and then went up to Ban Co Peak to watch the sunset. The views were amazing and the whole day was just brilliant.

We did a similar tour with another company last year in a jeep-style vehicle, but doing it on the back of a bike was so much more fun!

Our drivers, Xo and My, were fantastic. I’d never been on the back of a motorbike before and, with the busy traffic and some very steep roads, I was a little nervous at first. But I honestly felt 100% safe with them the whole time. They were both such confident and careful drivers and really made the experience for us.

They were a credit to the company and we couldn’t recommend them enough. If you’re thinking about doing the Hai Van Pass, definitely do it by bike with Mr T Easy Rider Tours! If you can personally request a driver My snd Xo were amazing, thank you 🏍️🇻🇳
